jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Bioinformatics
jobs.description:
Company Description

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant® is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. For more information, visit guardanthealth.com and follow the company on LinkedIn, X (Twitter) and Facebook.

Position Summary

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer, Bioinformatics to design, develop, and maintain scalable software solutions supporting bioinformatics, life sciences, and clinical diagnostic applications. This role is ideal for an experienced software engineer who combines strong full-stack development skills with an interest in applying modern software engineering and AI-assisted development practices to complex scientific and clinical workflows.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, collaborating with geographically distributed and cross-functional teams, and building high-quality software where reliability, traceability, and maintainability are essential.

Key Responsibilities

Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain robust software applications and services supporting bioinformatics and clinical workflows.
Build scalable backend services and APIs using Python and modern web frameworks such as Django and FastAPI.
Develop responsive and maintainable user interfaces using modern frontend technologies such as React.
Design and optimize relational data models and database solutions using PostgreSQL.
Architect, deploy, and operate applications and services in AWS environments.
Apply sound software engineering practices including automated testing, code reviews, CI/CD, observability, security, and infrastructure automation.
Partner with bioinformatics scientists, computational biologists, product managers, quality teams, and other stakeholders to translate scientific and business requirements into reliable software solutions.
Develop software capable of supporting complex scientific datasets, analytical workflows, and computational pipelines.
Use modern AI-assisted software development tools to improve engineering productivity, including code generation, code review, testing, debugging, technical documentation, and developer workflows.
Evaluate emerging AI development tools and establish effective practices for their responsible use within the software development lifecycle.
Produce clear technical documentation, architecture specifications, design documents, and operational procedures.
Contribute to architectural decisions and help establish software development standards and engineering best practices.
Troubleshoot complex production issues and drive root-cause analysis and long-term corrective solutions.
Work effectively across multiple time zones and with geographically distributed engineering, scientific, and business teams.
Mentor other engineers and contribute to the technical growth of the broader engineering organization.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
5+ years of professional software development experience, with significant hands-on development experience using Python.
Strong experience developing production applications using Python web frameworks such as Django, FastAPI, or similar technologies.
Experience developing modern web applications using React, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
Strong experience with relational databases, particularly PostgreSQL, including schema design, queries, performance optimization, and data integrity.
Hands-on experience developing, deploying, and supporting applications in AWS.
Strong understanding of RESTful APIs, distributed systems, service-oriented architectures, and modern application design principles.
Experience with automated testing, source control, code review, CI/CD, and modern DevOps practices.
Demonstrated experience using AI-enabled software engineering tools for activities such as coding, testing, debugging, code review, and documentation.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to work on complex technical problems with limited supervision.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment and effectively manage multiple priorities.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate successfully with geographically distributed and cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing software in life sciences, biotechnology, genomics, healthcare, or clinical diagnostics.
Familiarity with bioinformatics workflows, genomic data, computational pipelines, or scientific computing environments.
Experience developing software within a regulated environment, particularly systems subject to FDA requirements or other healthcare or life-sciences quality regulations.
Familiarity with software development practices supporting regulated products, including requirements traceability, design controls, verification and validation, change control, and documentation.
Experience with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
Experience with AWS services such as ECS/EKS, Lambda, RDS, S3, CloudWatch, IAM, and related cloud infrastructure.
Experience with infrastructure-as-code technologies such as Terraform or AWS CDK.
Experience designing systems that process large scientific or clinical datasets.
Familiarity with data privacy, security, and compliance considerations associated with clinical or healthcare data.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with an understanding of scientific and clinical workflows to deliver reliable, scalable applications. You will be expected to operate with a high degree of ownership, collaborate effectively across technical and scientific disciplines, and continuously identify ways to improve software quality and engineering productivity.

You will also help the organization thoughtfully adopt modern AI-enabled development practices while maintaining the engineering rigor, documentation, and quality standards required for software supporting life sciences and clinical applications.

AI & Digital Fluency

Demonstrate curiosity, sound judgment, and the ability to critically evaluate and responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools in accordance with company policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of work.

Hybrid Work Model:
This section is applicable to onsite employees who are eligible for hybrid work location as specified by management and related policies. Guardant has defined days for in-person/onsite collaboration and work-from-home days for individual-focused time. All U.S. employees who live within 50 miles of a Guardant facility will be required to be onsite on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays. We have found aligning our scheduled in-office days allows our teams to do the best work and creates the focused thinking time our innovative work requires. At Guardant, our work model has created flexibility for better work-life balance while keeping teams connected to advance our science for our patients.

The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below. This range does not include benefits or, if applicable, bonus, commission, or equity. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, education, job-related skills, job duties, and business need. Employee may be required to lift routine office supplies and use office equipment. Majority of the work is performed in a desk/office environment; however, there may be exposure to high noise levels, fumes, and biohazard material in the laboratory environment. Ability to sit for extended periods of time.

jobs.title: Staff Research Associate 1
jobs.description:
Department Summary

Research in the Department of Integrative Biology and Physiology (IBP) is dedicated to explaining the function of complex biological systems, in cells, organs, and individuals. The recent rapid advances in molecular and cell biology and genetics, including the sequencing of numerous genomes, has provided an unprecedented opportunity to use this new information to understand how the genes interact to produce emergent phenotypes in complex systems.

Position Summary

This position will require the staff research associate to perform coordination of research projects in the lab, which includes duties such as scheduling and screening participants, maintaining databases, attending and taking notes in lab meetings, and submitting IRB protocols. In particular, the associate will be the lead in collecting data for a BrightFocus Foundation Grant, which includes scheduling and screening participants, running the study that includes behavioral and neuropsychological testing as well as MRI and PET imaging and saliva sample collection. This position requires interacting professionally with participants across the lifespan (ages 18+), including older adults and those with neuropsychiatric conditions such as depression. Experience in working with human subjects or any experience with running neuroimaging studies or analyses is preferred but not required.

Salary & Compensation

UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.

Qualifications

Previous experience managing databases and demonstrated experience in managing several tasks, keeping all on track and organized. (Preferred)
Previous experience running participants or interacting with special populations (e.g. older adults, depression) (Preferred)
Experience with neuroimaging techniques, either on the data collection side or data analysis (Preferred)
Ability to use standard computer programming tools and databases (Excel, PsychoPy, Airtable) (Required)
Ability to maintain a laboratory record containing clear well-organized summaries of experiments and results. (Required)
Ability to maintain cooperative working relationships (Required)
Skill in communicating problems and information in a timely and critical manner. (Required)
Ability to conduct independent work once comfortable (Required)
Ability to teach others in lab, particularly undergraduate research assistants (Required)
Excellent organizational skills (Required)
Ability to work independently, supervise others, and follow through with tasks. (Required)
Personable and professional, especially when interacting with participants (Required)
Arrive early to prepare for study sessions with participants (Required)

Education, Licenses, Certifications & Personal Affiliations

Bachelor's Degree in related field (e.g. Psychology, Neuroscience), or equivalent experience/training. (Preferred)

Special Conditions for Employment

Background Check: Continued employment is contingent upon the completion of a satisfactory background investigation.

CANRA: The position is designated as a mandatory reporter under CANRA. The employee must sign the "Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse".
Clery Act: The position is a designated CSA (Campus Security Authority) under Clery Act requirements.

8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

jobs.title: Civil Engineering Intern – Transportation
jobs.description:
About Parametrix

Parametrix is a 100% employee-owned consulting firm helping clients deliver resilient infrastructure, vibrant and livable communities, and environmentally sustainable solutions. We are a team of professional construction managers, engineers, management consultants, planners, scientists, and surveyors dedicated to delivering outstanding client service. We build lasting partnerships and collaborate with our clients to envision possibilities and create tomorrow, together.

Recognized as a top workplace, we’re committed to a culture that values work-life balance, professional growth, and the well-being of our people.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for a Civil Engineering Intern
to join our Transportation team in Emeryville, California
. This is a great opportunity for a student interested in transportation engineering, roadway design, and complete streets to gain hands-on experience while working alongside experienced engineers and project teams.

We anticipate approximately 12–24 hours per week during the academic year
, with the opportunity to work full-time during summer and school breaks based on your interest and availability.

Our Emeryville team enjoys a collaborative, fun, and supportive office environment. Team members typically work in the office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and we would like our intern to spend some time in person on those days to support mentorship, learning, and team connections. We recognize the importance of balancing work with academic commitments and will work with you to establish a schedule that supports both.

At Parametrix, we believe internships should provide meaningful, real-world experience. You will have opportunities to contribute to actual projects, develop technical skills, and learn what it means to be a consulting engineer.

Many of our interns continue their careers with Parametrix after graduation, and we enjoy supporting their growth from students to engineering professionals.

Your Role on the Team:

Support civil engineering design for transportation facilities, roadway improvements, complete streets, and multimodal transportation projects.
Assist with the preparation of engineering plans, drawings, calculations, and technical documentation under the guidance of experienced engineers.
Gain exposure to roadway geometry, bicycle and pedestrian facilities, intersection improvements, and other transportation infrastructure.
Learn and develop skills using engineering design software, including AutoCAD Civil 3D and other relevant tools.
Collaborate with engineers, designers, and project managers to support project development and delivery.
Participate in project meetings, design reviews, and opportunities to learn about the engineering consulting process.
Gain exposure to real-world design challenges, project coordination, and the development of solutions that improve mobility and safety in our communities.

What You Bring to the Team:

Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Civil Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
Interest in transportation engineering, roadway design, complete streets, and multimodal transportation solutions.
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, or other engineering design tools is helpful but not required.
Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn from experienced professionals.

Why Join Parametrix?

Meaningful Experience:
Work on real transportation projects that help shape safer, more connected, and sustainable communities.

Great Mentors:
Learn from experienced engineers who are invested in your professional development and enjoy sharing their knowledge.

A Fun, Collaborative Team:
Join a welcoming office where people enjoy working together, sharing ideas, and supporting one another.

Flexibility for School:
Gain valuable professional experience while maintaining a schedule that supports your education, with opportunities for additional hours during summer and school breaks.

A Potential Path to Your Career:
We value building long-term relationships with our interns. Many have transitioned into full-time positions after graduation, continuing to grow their careers with Parametrix.

Employee Ownership:
Experience the culture of a 100% employee-owned company where collaboration, professional growth, and shared success are part of who we are.

If you're excited to put your classroom knowledge into practice, learn from great mentors, and contribute to transportation projects that make a difference, we'd love to hear from you!

Hourly Range: $30 USD - $32 USD

Compensation is determined by factors such as education, experience, location, and role. As employee-owners, we are eligible for performance-based bonuses and our salaries are reviewed annually. We value transparency and look forward to discussing our compensation structure.

Our Commitment to You

Parametrix is committed to being an inclusive workplace, where team members of all backgrounds and experiences are welcome. As an equal opportunity employer, it is our policy and culture to provide opportunities to all persons based on merit and fitness to perform job duties. Employment decisions are based solely on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, religion, age (40 or older, as protected under the ADEA), disability (including physical, mental, or sensory), genetic information (including testing and characteristics), protected veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws or regulations.

At Parametrix, we are dedicated to encouraging an inclusive and accessible workplace. If you need any accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know, and we will work with you to ensure your needs are met. We welcome and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Your Information Matters

In addition to your competitive salary, ICON offers a range of additional benefits. Our benefits are designed to be competitive within each country and are focused on well-being and work life balance opportunities for you and your family.

jobs.title: Part-time Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**About Jeevan**

Jeevan is a climate technology company developing novel carbon capture systems. Our work is hands-on, experimental, and fast-moving, with a strong emphasis on benchtop testing, prototyping, and data integrity. This role supports our core R&D efforts in our Alhambra facility.

**Role Overview**

This is a hands-on role combining bench-scale laboratory work with physical prototype assembly and test rig setup. The ideal candidate is comfortable both running controlled experiments and working with tools to build, modify, and troubleshoot small-scale systems. This role is well-suited to someone who enjoys building things as much as testing them.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Support Jeevan’s benchtop laboratory experiments under the direction of the Lab Director.
* Prepare common lab solutions and reagents based on target specifications (e.g., calculate and prepare solutions to a desired concentration, pH, and volume).
* Conduct routine bench-scale lab experiments following written instructions (e.g., resin/column tests, batch mixing, timed procedures), and proactively communicate questions or issues.
* Operate basic lab equipment as trained, including balances, pH meters, conductivity meters, stir plates, and peristaltic pumps; verify equipment is functioning properly prior to use.
* Collect, label, and store samples properly; perform basic measurements (pH, conductivity, mass, volume) and record results in a consistent format.
* Maintain clear, organized experimental notes (including dates, procedures, calculations, deviations, and observations) and upload data and photos to shared folders.
* Monitor experiments during runs (e.g., flow rate, leaks, temperature, system stability) and immediately document abnormalities or failures.
* Clean and organize work areas, glassware, and lab tools; manage routine lab waste disposal in accordance with safety guidelines.
* Contribute to experimental design and assist with equipment assembly and test setup.
* Maintain material and equipment inventory, including tracking supply needs and assisting with ordering or local pickup when required.
* Assemble and modify benchtop and pilot-scale test rigs, including tubing runs, fittings, pumps, filters, housings, and support frames.
* Use basic hand tools (wrenches, drills, saws, tubing cutters, etc.) to fabricate and adjust prototype components.
* Troubleshoot mechanical and fluid system issues (e.g., leaks, loose fittings, flow restrictions) and implement practical fixes.
* Assist in building and maintaining scale models and early-stage prototype systems.
* Support physical setup and teardown of experiments, including moving equipment and reconfiguring systems between test runs.

**Qualifications**

* Availability for 15 - 25 hours per week during standard working hours (8:00am–5:00pm ET).
* Ability to reliably commute to and from our lab at 1135 Westminster Ave, Unit K, Alhambra, CA.
* Prior laboratory experience (academic, research, or industry) preferred.
* Comfort working with basic lab equipment and following written experimental procedures.
* Strong attention to detail and willingness to document work clearly and consistently.
* Ability to work independently while communicating issues promptly and clearly.
* Prior experience with hands-on mechanical work, fabrication, or prototyping is strongly preferred.

**Work Authorization**

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States for the hours listed.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to stand for extended periods and perform hands-on lab work.
* Ability to lift and move light lab equipment and materials (generally under 25 lbs).
* Ability to safely handle lab materials while following safety protocols.

**How to Apply**

Please apply with:

* A brief introduction
* Your resume
* Your availability (days/times during the week)

Pay: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour

Expected hours: 15.0 – 25.0 per week

Work Location: In person

Company: Prodigy Labs

Location: San Diego, CA 92121

Schedule: Part-Time, 20–25 hours per week, Monday–Friday

Work Location: In Person

ABOUT THE POSITION

Prodigy Labs is seeking a reliable, detail-oriented Entry-Level Laboratory Technician to join our growing ISO/IEC 17025-accredited analytical testing laboratory in San Diego.

This hands-on position involves a combination of sample preparation, sample receiving and intake, inventory management, documentation, and general laboratory operations.

The ideal candidate is organized, dependable, and comfortable managing multiple responsibilities. While this is an entry-level position, applicants must have prior hands-on experience with pipetting, sample preparation, and basic laboratory procedures.

The technician will work closely with our analytical chemist and laboratory team and should be comfortable performing routine tasks independently after appropriate training.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Sample Preparation

* Prepare samples for HPLC and LC-MS/MS analysis according to established laboratory procedures.

* Perform accurate pipetting, weighing, dilutions, and solution preparation.

* Assist with peptide sample reconstitution and preparation of laboratory reagents and solutions.

* Prepare and organize autosampler vials according to laboratory worklists.

Sample Receiving and Documentation

* Receive, inspect, label, and log incoming laboratory samples.

* Verify sample information and maintain accurate chain-of-custody documentation.

* Enter and update sample information in laboratory tracking systems.

* Maintain accurate laboratory records and documentation.

Inventory Management

* Receive, label, track, and organize laboratory supplies, chemicals, and reagents.

* Monitor inventory levels and notify appropriate staff when supplies need to be reordered.

* Maintain accurate inventory records and assist with routine inventory checks.

* Receive and organize incoming laboratory supplies and deliveries.

General Laboratory Operations

* Assist with routine laboratory equipment checks and maintenance documentation.

* Maintain clean, organized, and safe laboratory work areas.

* Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs), safety protocols, and laboratory quality standards.

* Assist laboratory staff with additional operational and administrative tasks as needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* Coursework or a degree in chemistry, biochemistry, biology, or a related scientific field, or equivalent laboratory experience.

* Minimum 6 months of hands-on wet laboratory experience, including pipetting and sample preparation. Academic research and internship experience are acceptable.

* Experience using micropipettes and analytical balances.

* Knowledge of basic laboratory techniques, including weighing, dilutions, and solution preparation.

* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and accurate recordkeeping.

* Ability to follow written procedures and work independently after appropriate training and authorization.

* Basic computer skills for data entry, inventory management, and laboratory documentation.

* Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize daily responsibilities.

* Good communication skills and ability to work as part of a team.

* Availability to work Monday through Friday during scheduled hours.

PREFERRED BUT NOT REQUIRED

* Experience with HPLC or LC-MS/MS sample preparation.

* Familiarity with peptide or dietary supplement testing.

* Experience working in an ISO/IEC 17025, GLP, or GMP laboratory.

* Familiarity with laboratory inventory management or sample tracking systems.

WHAT WE OFFER

* Competitive hourly pay based on experience.

* Hands-on experience in a growing analytical testing laboratory.

* Training on laboratory-specific methods, equipment, and procedures.

* Opportunities to expand technical skills and take on additional laboratory responsibilities.

* Potential for professional growth within the company.

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Preclinical Pharmacology
jobs.description:
**Senior Research Associate, Preclinical Pharmacology**

*Run in vivo studies that move Nurix's degrader programs toward the clinic. You'll execute mouse efficacy, PK/PD, and mechanism-of-action studies in oncology and inflammation models and generate the Western blot and flow cytometry data that show how our molecules work.*

**Position Description**

**The Opportunity**

* Join the Research – Preclinical Pharmacology team as a full-time, onsite, hands-on member, reporting to a Scientist / Principal Scientist, Preclinical Pharmacology
* Perform mouse handling and in-life procedures, including dosing by oral (PO), intraperitoneal (IP), subcutaneous (SC), and intravenous (IV) routes, tumor cell implantation, tumor and body-weight measurements, and in-life and terminal blood collection
* Execute PK/PD, tolerability, and efficacy studies in oncology xenograft/syngeneic models and in murine models of inflammation, under the direction of study leads
* Prepare and formulate test articles and vehicles for dosing; monitor animal health, document observations, and escalate adverse events promptly
* Perform necropsy and collect, process, and bank tissues and blood for downstream biomarker and pharmacodynamic analyses
* Prepare tissue and cell lysates and perform Western blotting (including quantitative and automated capillary formats) to measure target degradation and pathway modulation
* Develop, run, and analyze multi-color flow cytometry panels for immune and tumor-cell phenotyping from blood, spleen, tumor, and other tissues
* Maintain and expand cell lines using sterile cell culture technique; support cell-based assays and the generation of cells for in vivo implantation
* Record experiments accurately and in a timely manner in the electronic lab notebook; analyze, graph, and summarize data and present results at team meetings
* Collaborate with Biology, Chemistry, DMPK, and Translational teams to design studies and troubleshoot models and assays
* Adhere to IACUC protocols, animal welfare regulations, and laboratory safety requirements, and maintain required training and certifications
* Contribute to the optimization and qualification of new models and assays and to the training of junior team members
* Maintain laboratory equipment and supplies and support vivarium coordination, including occasional weekend or off-shift study coverage; other essential duties as assigned; minimal travel (<5%)

**What You'll Bring**

* BS/MS in Biology, Pharmacology, Immunology, Cancer Biology, or a related field, with a BS or equivalent plus 8 or more years of relevant experience, or an MS plus 4 or more years of relevant experience
* Industry (biotech or pharma) experience conducting in vivo pharmacology studies in mice
* Proficiency in mouse handling and dosing by PO, IP, SC, and IV routes, as well as blood collection and tissue harvest
* Hands-on experience with oncology models (e.g., xenograft, syngeneic) and with murine models of inflammation or immunology
* Demonstrated proficiency in Western blotting and flow cytometry, including sample preparation, staining, and data analysis
* Proficiency in sterile mammalian cell culture technique
* Working knowledge of IACUC regulations and humane animal care practices
* Strong organizational and documentation skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple studies simultaneously
* Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable in a fast-paced, team-oriented research environment
* Ability to work in an animal facility and tolerate exposure to laboratory animals, and to work occasional weekends or off-shift hours as studies require
* Bonus: experience with targeted protein degradation (molecular glues, PROTACs) or other small-molecule oncology or immunology programs
* Bonus: experience with multi-spectral flow cytometry, automated Western (e.g., Jess/Wes), ELISA, or MSD cytokine/biomarker assays
* Bonus: experience with orthotopic, disseminated, PDX, or humanized mouse models, or with in vivo imaging
* Bonus: experience with inflammation models such as collagen-induced arthritis, colitis, or cytokine-challenge models
* Bonus: familiarity with PK/PD relationships, compound formulation, and dose-response study design
* Bonus: proficiency with GraphPad Prism and electronic lab notebook systems

**Salary Range:** $131,400 - $139,900

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

  

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine's next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.*

About The Role

What if your native German fluency could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a doctor's office? We're looking for native German speakers based in the New York area to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

New York's large German-speaking community — from recent expats to heritage speakers — makes it an ideal place to find people with the authentic, natural German speech this project demands. You'll role-play as a patient using fictional personas we provide, record short conversations, and grade the AI's performance.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role for people with clear German speech, strong attention to detail, and an ear for what sounds natural and fluent.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Contract (task-based)
Location: Remote
Commitment: Flexible, work at your own pace

What You'll Do

Hold 4 to 5 minute spoken conversations in German with an AI front desk assistant, playing a fictional patient
Say natural trigger phrases to test whether the AI makes the correct function calls — for example, checking a patient record, booking an appointment, or verifying insurance
Review transcripts and classify how accurately the AI understood you and responded
Flag issues such as mispronunciations, cutoffs, interruptions, delays, and incorrect function calls, including timestamps
Test how the AI handles background noise, short replies such as "ja," "nein," or "okay," long numbers, emotional moments, and sensitive or unsafe requests

Native or near-native German speaker with a clear, natural speaking voice

Able to follow multi-step instructions and apply them consistently

Comfortable using web-based tools

Experience in voice AI evaluation, data annotation, or QA testing
Background in healthcare administration, customer service, or call centre work
Familiarity with spoken German variants from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
Linguistics or language-focused academic background
Familiarity with medical terminology in German

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Task-based work with real autonomy
Directly help make voice AI more accurate, natural, and safe in healthcare settings
Potential for ongoing work as new projects launch

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Sarmal, Inc. is a San Diego–based biotechnology company developing next-generation genomics and molecular detection platforms. Our work integrates molecular biology, chemistry, and advanced systems engineering to enable faster, more precise, and more accessible genomic insights.

We are a highly collaborative, R&D-driven team operating in a fast-paced, early-stage environment. Our scientists and engineers work across disciplines to solve complex technical challenges and translate innovation into scalable, real-world applications.

At Sarmal, we value scientific rigor, curiosity, and a builder mindset. We are looking for individuals who are energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and excited to help bring breakthrough technologies from concept to reality.

About The Job

Sarmal is seeking a Research Technician to support routine batch execution and core analytical measurements for a biosensor device platform's surface chemistry processes. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role — running defined procedures under direct RA/scientist supervision, maintaining careful documentation, and building toward greater independence over time. Suited to candidates with foundational lab experience (academic, co-op, or early industry); strong execution and reliability may open the door to broader involvement in experimental support work as the program progresses. Open to early-career candidates with relevant hands-on lab training; not intended for a fully independent, self-directed hire.

Key Responsibilities

Execute surface functionalization batch runs (SAM, silane, hydrogel, brush polymer chemistries) per written SOPs/batch records, under direct RA/scientist supervision.
Operate the team's core surface characterization methods — fluorescence-based uniformity assays and contact angle — for routine batch checks, with EIS/CV support as trained.
Record characterization results (thickness, density, uniformity, charge) accurately and completely for RA/scientist review.
Assist with surface deposition/patterning process runs (spin-coating, dip-coating, spray-coating, plasma treatment/activation; exposure to PE-CVD/CVD or photolithographic patterning a plus).
Prepare samples and run defined test conditions for DOE test plans as directed by RA/scientist staff.
Log data accurately and promptly in lab notebooks/ELN; flag deviations from expected process parameters to RA/scientist staff.
Maintain organized inventory of chemistry consumables and reagents used in daily runs.
Maintain cleanroom/lab space per site protocols.
Work collaboratively with in-house RAs and scientists; follow established procedures precisely and escalate issues rather than resolving independently.

Qualifications

Hands-on lab experience (academic or industry) with interfacial materials or related wet-chemistry techniques; comfort executing established analytical methods (e.g., contact angle, fluorescence-based assays) with training.
Ability to follow detailed written procedures (SOPs, batch records) precisely and consistently.
Strong attention to detail and reliability; comfortable following defined test procedures exactly as written in a fast-paced environment.
Comfort with structured documentation (batch records, ELN, GDP-style recordkeeping).

Education

B.S. in Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Biology, or related field (or equivalent hands-on lab training) + 0–2 years of relevant lab experience — academic, or industry — with surface chemistry, thin-film processes, or related wet-chemistry techniques

Benefits & Perks

Sarmal offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
Company-paid life insurance
401(k) retirement plan
Generous paid time off
Access to additional voluntary benefits, employee perks, and discount programs
We are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees and providing a strong foundation for both professional and personal success.

ABOUT US:
The VERBIO Nevada Biorefinery
, located in Nevada, Iowa (USA), is the first industrial scale renewable natural gas (RNG) facility in North America using agricultural residues as its feedstock. The plant is 100% owned by VERBIO North America Holdings Corporation. RNG production from corn stover began in December 2021 with the completion of Phase I, at a capacity of 7 million ethanol gallons equivalent (EGE) per year. Upon completion of Phase II in the 4th quarter of 2022, the site will begin operating as a biorefinery, producing 60 million gallons of corn-based ethanol and an additional 19 million (EGE) of RNG from stillage. The integration of RNG and ethanol production, unique to VERBIO, incorporates advanced operational technology currently practiced at the company’s facilities in Germany. The process also yields humus, a soil amendment, and organic fertilizers. VERBIO Vereinigte BioEnergie AG (VERBIO AG)
, with headquarters in Leipzig, Germany, is a leading independent manufacturer of biofuels and bioenergy in Germany and Europe. The company began producing biofuel in 2001 and today has approximately 900 employees at its locations in Germany, Poland, Hungary, India, USA and Canada producing biodiesel, bioethanol and biomethane (renewable natural gas), as well as feed, bio-fertilizers and other high-value by-products for the nutrition, pharmaceutical and cosmetics industries, all on an industrial scale. VERBIO concentrates on the use of internally developed innovative and efficient energy-saving production processes. With its innovative processes and highly efficient production plants, VERBIO is a technology leader in the biofuels market. VNA plans to build, own, operate, and finance biofuel facilities across the United States and Canada. Our Vision
Energy production from renewable resources is the key component of the world’s future energy mix. Renewable raw materials have the potential to permanently replace fossil fuels and simultaneously solve the problem of surplus agricultural production in North America and elsewhere. It is VERBIO’s goal to be a leader in 21st century alternative green energy solutions. As we consolidate and expand our position as one of the world’s leading biofuels producers, we will leverage our technologies and the value of agriculture to create renewable and sustainable solutions globally, while pursing solid growth and responsible relationships with our stakeholders: farmers, customers, employees, shareholders, partners, researchers, consumers, governmental entities, and interest groups. Our Mission
VERBIO North America is committed to the principle of sustainability and treats natural resources in a socially responsible and ethical manner. Using the latest technologies, developed in-house, we are creating sustainable alternatives for a world whose desire is to move away from fossil fuels. Our business model endeavors to ignite change and create platforms where the path to green energy is contagious. With our fuels cutting greenhouse gas emissions by up to 90% compared to fossil fuels, we are showing the way forward in climate protection. And with a vision for a greener future, we are building strong competence centers and competitive production facilities in different parts of the world, while our employees partner alongside farmers to safeguard the environment for current and future generations. Our Approach

Be creative, innovative, ethical, and fast in execution.
Partner with agriculture to safeguard land and natural resources for future generations.
Create enthusiasm around sustainability and renewable energy production.
Empower employees to develop & execute upon big ideas.
Be good citizens in our local & global communities.
Never stop technological improvement.

Sarmal, Inc. is a San Diego–based biotechnology company developing next-generation genomics and molecular detection platforms. Our work integrates molecular biology, chemistry, and advanced systems engineering to enable faster, more precise, and more accessible genomic insights.

This role requires hands-on experience in an industrial organic chemistry lab setting, and the chemist should be comfortable working with sensitive compounds and complex purification and QC analysis techniques. This chemist will contribute to development of crucial upstream materials that will pillar the core technology at Sarmal.  

Key Responsibilities

Synthesize modified nucleosides/nucleotides using a variety of synthesis techniques.

Characterize compounds using analytical techniques including LC-MS, NMR, IR, UV/Vis, TLC, and related methods.
Optimize reaction conditions and develop analytical methods to produce high-quality compounds that meet project requirements.
Maintain accurate and detailed electronic laboratory notebooks and manage inventory of synthesized compounds and related materials.
Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory equipment and analytical instrumentation.
Analyze and interpret experimental data and present findings at project and departmental meetings.

Qualifications

Strong understanding of modern organic chemistry techniques in literature and in laboratory. 
Hands-on experience organic chemistry synthesis techniques including air- and moisture-sensitive reactions using Schlenk techniques and inert atmosphere conditions.
Proficiency in operating analytical instrumentation such as HPLC and LC-MS with the ability to interpret results from data acquisition. 
Strong analytical chemistry skills using LC-MS, NMR, IR, UV/Vis, TLC, and related techniques.
Experience in chemoenzymatic reactions is a plus.
Strong documentation and scientific communication skills.
Strong sense of teamwork, flexibility, and enthusiasm for advancing new technologies. 

Education

B.S. or M.S. in organic chemistry, nucleotide/nucleic acid chemistry, bioorganic chemistry, or related discipline.
5–8 years post-B.S. or 2-4 years post-M.S. of relevant industry experience in organic chemistry, nucleic acid chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or related fields.

jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: Engineering Specialist

LOCATION: San Francisco or Sacramento

JOB OPENING #: 6780

OVERVIEW 

The Judicial Council of California is accepting applications for the position of Engineering Specialist (Energy & Sustainability) with the Facilities Services office.

The Engineering Specialist will be responsible for analyzing and validating utility data, including electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels, for courthouses in the assigned regions in Central and Southern California. The role supports sustainability-focused decision-making by identifying usage trends, verifying billing accuracy, and flagging inefficiencies. A significant focus is on maintaining high-quality data in platforms such as ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the Energy Management Information System (EMIS) to support energy reduction, water conservation, and decarbonization goals.

The Engineering Specialist supports the monthly and annual reporting of energy and water use, costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, as well as regulatory compliance reporting, including GHG inventory data compilation and support for Assembly Bill (AB) 802 benchmarking. Trend analysis to identify peak demand, abnormal water use, and inefficiencies is a key aspect of this work.

This position also involves conducting or supporting energy and water audits, life cycle cost analysis, and technical reviews of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems in support of energy efficiency, water efficiency, and waste reduction upgrades and capital project planning. The Engineering Specialist helps identify and track utility incentives and rebates, recommends energy- and water-efficient equipment, and contributes to the development of energy, water conservation, and waste reduction policy. The position serves as the technical water and waste resource for the Sustainability Unit and provides related educational training for the field staff and court staff.

The Judicial Council 

The Judicial Council of California is the policy setting body for the state court system and has constitutionally conferred statewide rule-making authority. This authority includes developing, advocating for, and allocating the judicial branch budget. A majority of Council members are California state justices and judges; however, the Council also includes lawyers, legislators, and court administrators.

By enhancing its role as a leadership, knowledge, and service resource for the judicial branch, the Judicial Council’s staff organization seeks to continue to evolve as one of California’s most dynamic public service entities, focused on improving access to justice for all Californians by innovating and responding to the changing needs of the courts and the public. As a government body charged with improving the statewide administration of justice, the Judicial Council has multiple offices with diverse responsibilities relating to court policy and operations. As employees of the council, every member of staff should view and approach their work as one Judicial Council with a public service mission that is greater than the sum of its parts.

The Judicial Council strives for work-life balance, including substantial vacation and holiday time. In addition, we offer an excellent benefits package, including pension, medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible spending, up to $130 per month reimbursement for qualifying commuting costs, student loan forgiveness as part of Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and retirement savings plans. In San Francisco, the office is only a 7-minute walk from the Civic Center BART station. In Sacramento, the office is minutes from downtown, just north of Discovery Park.

The Judicial Council offers hybrid work arrangements for many positions. The successful candidate will be expected to work in person at the Judicial Council’s San Francisco or Sacramento office at least two days per week, based on their office leader’s direction, and reside in the areas surrounding these locations. To be eligible for Judicial Council employment and participation in the Judicial Council’s Hybrid Work Program, a prospective or current employee’s primary residence/remote work location must be in the State of California and within a 150-mile driving radius of their assigned reporting location.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Review and validate utility bills for electricity, natural gas, water, waste, and fuels for courthouses in the assigned regions, including daily batch reviews, late bill monitoring, and accurate entry of paper and electronic invoices in the EMIS.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS

OTHER

jobs.title: AI Trainer - PHYSICS
jobs.description:
About The Role

Our client is looking for experienced scientists and engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real technical work: analyzing test, measurement or process data, sizing and verifying a design, designing an experiment and reading it out, interpreting a simulation, writing the technical report. You bring the judgment you have built catching the unit error in a test file, the multiple comparisons trap in a process improvement study, and the assumption that does not hold at the boundary. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a calculation package with stated assumptions and checks, a test plan and data analysis, a failure or deviation investigation, a design trade study, an experimental protocol with acceptance criteria, a circuit or system design review, or a technical report, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

Across our STEM and Data Science programs, tasks are grounded in real day-to-day workflows and checked against frontier models so only genuinely hard tasks make it through. Some projects are authored and verified in code, so coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on those projects.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional science or engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long-form and self-directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic technical tasks drawn from your own day-to-day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer or scientist would need (test data, drawings or schematics, specifications, simulation outputs, lab records, reports), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, analysis, design review or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain (the right assumptions stated, the right method, the right magnitudes and units, the right failure modes considered), and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unit and scaling errors, misread data, unsupported conclusions, fabricated or ignored source files, missed safety or boundary conditions, and off-brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your discipline and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other experts.

Qualifications

2+ years of applied experience preferred in one of the core sciences (mathematics, physics, chemistry, or biology) or in an engineering discipline (electrical and electronics, civil and structural, materials, chemical and process, environmental and earth sciences, or similar) or in data science.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher. We prefer 2+ years of experience outside undergraduate study.
Coding / scientific computing is a strong plus and is required on some projects: comfortable writing and verifying work in code (Python or similar) and working at the command line.
Hands-on with real data and the tools of your field: instrument and test data, measurement files, simulation outputs, schematics or drawings, and the analysis tools that go with them (MATLAB, Python or R; SPICE and PCB tools; FEA or CFD; GIS; chromatography or spectroscopy software).
Comfort with statistical and experimental reasoning: experiment design, measurement error and uncertainty, and the common statistical traps. The assessment leans on this.
Working understanding of adjacent sub-disciplines, enough to assess work outside your own specialty and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Hands-on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual-contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native-level written and spoken English; you can articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools: you can tell a well-reasoned answer from a plausible-sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Advanced degree or professional licensure (PE, chartered status) is a plus but not required. Practical applied work outweighs credentials.

The company operates in the SaaS, hospitality, media, and marketing industries, with a focus on understanding how clients appear in AI-generated answers and how that visibility influences business outcomes. The team has approximately 50 employees.

About the Role

The company is looking for a Sr. Data Analyst to lead analytics and research into AI search visibility, source citations, content performance, and the relationship between AI-generated recommendations and measurable business results. Reporting to the Vice President of Product, you will help establish reliable methods for measuring how often clients appear in AI answers, how they compare with competitors, and what factors influence those results.

This role combines data analytics, research, experimentation, and LLM evaluation. You will work with structured and unstructured data, develop measurement frameworks, evaluate AI search systems, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to define meaningful metrics. The focus is on producing reliable, transparent findings that help clients understand their performance and identify areas for improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Track how frequently, favorably, and accurately clients appear in AI-generated answers compared with defined competitors, using rigorous baselines, sampling methods, and documented uncertainty.
Maintain tracked-prompt panels across AI engines, topics, and markets, and report changes in visibility over time.
Identify and analyze the sources cited by AI systems for specific topics, including the composition of those sources.
Measure how published content becomes cited evidence in AI answers, how long it takes to appear, and how long citations persist.
Identify gaps in clients' evidence bases and determine what content or sources may be missing.
Test how content characteristics, including source, framing, format, specificity, recency, and structure, affect the likelihood of being cited by AI systems.
Connect AI visibility metrics with referral traffic, engagement, bookings, and conversions, identifying what can be measured reliably and where the connection between recommendations and revenue breaks down.
Evaluate AI-generated answers for accuracy, relevance, and completeness, documenting recurring failure modes across engines.
Maintain evaluation rubrics, benchmarks, and processes for measuring agreement between raters.
Refine prompt construction methods and apply consistent evaluation standards to internally developed AI features.
Research how AI search systems retrieve and cite sources, validating findings through research rather than relying on industry commentary.
Work with product and engineering teams to define product metrics and ensure every customer-facing figure can be reproduced from documented inputs.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in analytics, data science, research, and/or search products.

Hands-on fluency with large language models (LLMs) and agentic tooling, including prompt design, evaluation harnesses, and agents that collect and process data at scale.
Strong SQL and Python skills.
Experience designing experiments using observational data, including comparison group construction, difference-in-differences or matched comparisons, and appropriate consideration of statistical power.

Startup experience is required, including working in fast-moving, small teams with a high level of ownership and visibility.

The compensation package includes a base salary of $120,000–$140,000, plus equity and an annual bonus.

The Opportunity

Join the Research – Preclinical Pharmacology team as a full-time, onsite, hands-on member, reporting to a Scientist / Principal Scientist, Preclinical Pharmacology
Perform mouse handling and in-life procedures, including dosing by oral (PO), intraperitoneal (IP), subcutaneous (SC), and intravenous (IV) routes, tumor cell implantation, tumor and body-weight measurements, and in-life and terminal blood collection
Execute PK/PD, tolerability, and efficacy studies in oncology xenograft/syngeneic models and in murine models of inflammation, under the direction of study leads

Collaborate with Biology, Chemistry, DMPK, and Translational teams to design studies and troubleshoot models and assays
Adhere to IACUC protocols, animal welfare regulations, and laboratory safety requirements, and maintain required training and certifications
Contribute to the optimization and qualification of new models and assays and to the training of junior team members
Maintain laboratory equipment and supplies and support vivarium coordination, including occasional weekend or off-shift study coverage; other essential duties as assigned; minimal travel (

BS/MS in Biology, Pharmacology, Immunology, Cancer Biology, or a related field, with a BS or equivalent plus 8 or more years of relevant experience, or an MS plus 4 or more years of relevant experience
Industry (biotech or pharma) experience conducting in vivo pharmacology studies in mice
Proficiency in mouse handling and dosing by PO, IP, SC, and IV routes, as well as blood collection and tissue harvest
Hands-on experience with oncology models (e.g., xenograft, syngeneic) and with murine models of inflammation or immunology
Demonstrated proficiency in Western blotting and flow cytometry, including sample preparation, staining, and data analysis
Proficiency in sterile mammalian cell culture technique
Working knowledge of IACUC regulations and humane animal care practices
Strong organizational and documentation skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple studies simultaneously
Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable in a fast-paced, team-oriented research environment

Bonus: experience with targeted protein degradation (molecular glues, PROTACs) or other small-molecule oncology or immunology programs
Bonus: experience with multi-spectral flow cytometry, automated Western (e.g., Jess/Wes), ELISA, or MSD cytokine/biomarker assays

Bonus: proficiency with GraphPad Prism and electronic lab notebook systems

Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix’s dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Policy Research Associate will support the evaluation, prioritization and advancement of state and local policies that can provide effective and scalable contributions to the adoption of regenerative agriculture practices and water quality improvements across the country, primarily though not exclusively at the state level. They will work with interdisciplinary teams to identify, compile, and research promising water policy interventions, develop legislative or administrative solutions for those interventions, and work with government relations professionals and others to implement those solutions at the state or federal level. The Research Associate will help identify and foster relationships with third-party contractors, including consultants, other NGOs, universities, among others to build TNC’s policy research capabilities.

Responsibilities & Scope

May supervise administrative staff and/or volunteers, interns, or temporary staff.
Financial responsibility to complete projects appropriately and assist with budget development and meeting fundraising goals for local and worldwide conservation.
Ensures program compliance with internal policies and external requirements.
Works within scope of program’s strategic goals.
Provides research and policy analysis in support of legislative and/or policy priorities.
May aid with preparation of program materials including presentations, memos, and other communications.
Influences the outcome of policy and/or corporate initiatives at the federal, state, and local levels.
Develop strategic partnerships with relevant agencies, conservation organizations, and/or industry.
Work independently, working with supervisor as needed.
May require occasional domestic travel for multi-day retreats, meetings, and conferences
May work long/flexible hours as needed to coordinate with staff and partners across the US or region.

This is a full-time, 2-year grant-funded position with the possibility of extension based on continued grant funding. Working location is remote from a home office within the continental United States.

We’re Looking For You

The Policy Research Associate will play a vital role in the development and support of replicable policy interventions at the state and local level to advance the outcomes of the North America Agriculture Program’s Water Policy Accelerator. They will serve as a subject matter expert on projects with other teams and will be responsible for assisting our government relations staff in advancing interventions to water quality challenges. A priority area for this work will be to research and design policy interventions that expand the implementation of Edge of Field practices, such as vegetative buffers and wetlands, as well as identifying and developing policy solutions to other water policy challenges. This position will report into the North America Agriculture Program, working closely with an interdisciplinary team from North America Policy and Government Relations, Global Conservation Campaigns, numerous state Business Units, and external stakeholders. The Policy Research Associate will have strong analytical skills, experience in policy analysis, and an understanding of law and the legislative process. The successful candidate will be able to work effectively independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, highly matrixed organization; and be adaptable to shifting needs and priorities.

What You’ll Bring

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree and 3 years related experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Fluency in English
Experience researching information from divergent sources and compiling it into a cohesive reporting structure.
Experience with legislative or policy initiatives at the state level.
Experience presenting to and communicating with government or corporate staff and/or program leadership.
Experience working with partners and government agencies.

Desired Qualifications:
Juris Doctor Degree or Master’s Degree in Public Policy or related field.
Experience drafting legislation and negotiating with interested parties.
Experience developing or implementing federal or state policies, including funding/grant programs.
Experience with programs, laws and stakeholders who engage on agriculture, water and land-use policy related work in the United States.

Salary Information

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $60,000 - $85,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

Millions of people rely on digital maps every day to navigate, to discover, to find their way. Accurately verified mapping data prevents real-world navigation errors. Tuesday - Saturday: 2pm - 10:30pm (PM Shift)

A key part of the role is supervising team members and ensuring that all laboratory procedures are followed for specimen handling, next-generation sequencing (NGS) processes, test analyses, and the accurate maintenance of patient records.

In our lab, we foster a positive, friendly, and team-based environment. We all pitch in to achieve our common goals and support each other. Extractions
Library Preparation
Enrichments
Sequencing

Select, implement, and evaluate quality control materials for statistical process control of laboratory assays.
Troubleshoot assays and equipment when quality control materials fail to perform as expected.
Document all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from established performance specifications.
Assist in audits by regulatory bodies like CAP and external customers.
Participate in activities that support the laboratory's necessary licensure, including quality management and on-site inspections.
Identify and correct problems that may negatively affect test performance or result reporting. If a problem cannot be immediately corrected, notify a supervisor, clinical consultant, or director.
Train other CLS and lab personnel on laboratory methods.
Monitor the activities of non-licensed staff.
Provide guidance to team members on troubleshooting and deviation investigations.
Assist in assay development activities.
Demonstrate strong analytical skills and independent critical thinking.
Apply technical and functional knowledge to help the team meet its goals.
Work independently to identify and resolve complex, open-ended problems.

Licensure: Valid California Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) or Clinical Genetic Molecular Biologist Scientist (CGMBS) license.

Position Summary

Assist the Multiuse Laboratory Supervisor and/or Director in the overseeing of the Multiuse laboratories in support of National University academic programs. In addition, is the first point of contact for students and organizational escalations.

Essential Functions

Act as the auxiliary supervisor for all Multiuse Laboratories within the National University System.
Supervise the preparations for laboratory experiments and demonstrations for scheduled classes in close collaboration with university faculty.
Assist with and train multiuse laboratory staff on experiment set-ups. Assist instructors and students during laboratory classes.
Provide monthly and long-term laboratory schedules to campus directors, SoALS and resolve scheduling conflicts.
Develop a hands-on operating guide for the SeqStudio genetic analyzer, and keep it updated when forensic procedures change.
Develop a hands-on operating guide for the Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography (UPLC) for chemical separation and analysis.
Add procedures for confirmatory testing of when chemical materials are added to the forensic curriculum.

Provide escalation support and first level conflict resolution.
Lead department meetings.
Hold 1:1s with team members and provide skills coaching.
Team oversight and coverage support in the absence of the Multiuse Laboratory Supervisor and/or Director
Remediation committee team member for performance management.

Coach and provide feedback for team members on lab and chemical preparation and safety
Support front line team members through safety changes as well as course changes and all things involved with being able to teach those courses

Provide support and coverage for team as needed.

Other duties as assigned.

Indirect oversight of up to 6 front line team members.
Coaching, performance support and feedback, outcome delivery, process management, and team member training required.

Education & Experience:

Bachelor's degree in science-related field of study required; and, two to four (2-4) years of experience in science laboratory techniques and concepts in the areas of life, physical, and forensics sciences, safety regulations and procedures in science laboratories.
Manage teams of technicians at the Spectrum, South Bay, Naval Hospital, Fresno, and Los Angeles locations.
Provide lab technicians training on the operation and maintenance of all laboratory equipment using written, Zoom sessions, and onsite visits.
Provide training on Aseptic techniques, bacterial culturing, and sterile bacterial media preparation to all technicians.

Operation and maintenance of SeqStudio Genetic Analysis, UPLC chromatography, PCR, electrophoresis, physiology workstations, microscopes, FT-IR and UV-VIS spectrophotometry.

Ability to effectively and efficiently communicate organizational goals and deadlines to team members.

Ability to provide support in the hiring and training process of new team members.
Ability to coach to skill improvement and outcome development.
Strong understanding of all degree programs, specializations, and courses.
Ability to stay current via self-study on university policies, including policy update

Strong understanding of Natural Science and science laboratory operations/vernacular.
Strong written and verbal skills, organization, and follow-through.
Attention to detail.
Ability to use science laboratory tools and equipment required to support a typical university level academic environment/curriculum.
Function as university laboratory operations and safety expert and achieve compliance with external and internal safety policies and procedures.
Achieve compliance with regulations regarding storage/use/disposal of HAZMAT and BIOHAZ material. Establish new vendor contracts and maintain current vendor agreements and warranties.
Solves problems and develops relationships through shared goal of providing optimum learning environment for university students.
Ability to participate as an active team member of the team and organization and work toward a common goal.
Accepts personal accountability, proactively seeks resolution for personal limitations head-on; and supports honesty and respect towards others, the company and oneself.
Work independently and foster a cooperative spirit within a large and/or small team of diverse cultures, while working in a fast-paced environment with multiple projects, deadlines, and frequently changing priorities.

In this role, you will own the data ecosystem spanning the entire clinician lifecycle—from the moment a provider enters our recruiting funnel, through onboarding, credentialing, and state licensing, to their ongoing clinical performance, operational efficiency, and downstream business impact on patient retention.

You will develop performance frameworks that merge operational SLAs (e.g., on-time arrival, inbox turnaround times) with clinical quality and safety metrics. Additionally, you will lead our efforts in provider interaction analytics, creating evaluation and scoring logic to quantify qualitative behavioral dimensions, such as clinician empathy from consultation transcripts. Sitting at the intersection of Clinical Operations, Quality, Talent, Business Strategy, and Product, you will serve as the primary analytical partner to our Clinical Leadership and Executive team.

What You’ll Do

Credentialing & Licensing Efficiency:
Build predictive frameworks and monitoring dashboards to reduce state-by-state licensing bottlenecks and decrease provider time-to-first-consultation.

Technical Skills

Advanced skills in Python for statistical analysis, cohort modeling, survival analysis, and text/sentiment processing.

Proven ability to design intuitive, executive-ready dashboards in modern BI tools (e.g., Looker, Tableau, PowerBI).

Familiarity with text mining, sentiment analysis, or prompt-based LLM evaluation frameworks for processing qualitative data (transcripts, chat logs, survey notes).
Modern Analytics Stack & AI Tools:
Experience with cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) and active adoption of modern AI tools (e.g., LLMs for coding efficiency, automated insights) to accelerate analytics workflows.

Experience with cohort analysis, retention modeling, and constructing behavioral/qualitative scoring models.

Ability to take unstructured business and clinical questions and translate them into rigorous, answerable quantitative frameworks.

Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with non-technical stakeholders, particularly Clinical Lead/Medical Directors, Operations leads, and Talent teams.

jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila’s mission is to accelerate scientific discovery with AI, and that depends on trustworthy scientific data. As a Data Engineer, you’ll build ETL pipelines and data models for Lila’s scientific data platform, working at the intersection of data engineering, computational biology, chemistry, and materials science.

You’ll partner with AI researchers and experimentalists to turn raw lab instrument outputs into validated, analysis-ready datasets. The core challenge is data modeling: transforming messy, per-instrument measurements into clean, well-typed data that is efficient to query, reliable to use, and ready for downstream analysis.

You’ll also build domain-specific analysis functions and reusable data pipelines that help scientists and AI researchers move faster without re-deriving bespoke solutions.

What You'll Be Building

Design pipelines that turn raw lab output into analysis-ready scientific data.
Model heterogeneous data from bio, chemistry, and materials instruments.
Build validation checks, schema-evolution gates, and data quality workflows.
Develop reusable analysis functions for scientific and AI research workflows.
Improve automation and observability across instrument-to-result data flows.
Build canonical datasets that scientists and AI researchers can trust.
Use AI coding tools to accelerate pipeline development and team velocity.

What You'll Need To Succeed

2–6 years of experience in data engineering, bioinformatics, cheminformatics, or computational science. Strong Python skills, including typed, tested, production-quality code.
Strong SQL skills, especially with Postgres or similar relational databases.
Experience building ETL pipelines, data models, and reusable data transformations.
Data science foundation, including statistics and pandas, NumPy, or similar tools.
Experience translating noisy scientific measurements into accurate, validated datasets.
Workflow orchestration experience, ideally Flyte, Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, or Nextflow.
Active use of AI coding tools in day-to-day engineering work.

Bonus Points For

Experience with columnar or lakehouse stacks such as Parquet, Iceberg, DuckDB, Polars, or Ibis.
Familiarity with event-driven pipelines such as NATS or Kafka.
Exposure to lab instrument data formats, LIMS, or ELN systems.
Familiarity with life sciences assays, sequencing, imaging, or flow cytometry.
Familiarity with materials or chemistry methods such as XRD, XRF, SEM, TGA, or DSC.
Experience with curve fitting, peak detection, or unit and dimensional analysis.
