jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

At the Mission Payloads Division (MPD), we are pioneers in remote sensing systems that guide our country’s space enterprise. Our talented and dynamic people create and flourish in electronics, sensors, radar, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced data network domains. We boldly advance technology through our research and development and then forward to demonstration and integration. With innovative laboratories and prototyping, MPD delivers groundbreaking results. We guide our Department of Defense, intelligence community, and civil clients to enhance national productivity and security and tackle the most critical missions. Bring your intelligence and creative spirit and join us at MPD!

The Nuclear Hardness & Survivability (NH&S) department resides within MPD. Our staff includes technical leaders and subject matter experts in the areas of radiation survivability of electronic components/ hardware units in a natural and man-made space environment. Our expertise, combined with modeling and analysis capabilities, enables NH&S to deliver trusted assessments and recommendations to national security space systems and commercial customers. Take this opportunity to apply to the Aerospace NH&S department for the opportunity to work on cutting edge science with immediate mission impact.

The selected candidate will be required to work full time on-site at our facility at either Chantilly, VA; or El Segundo, CA.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead Nuclear Hardness and Survivability (NH&S) analyses for satellite electronics units, subsystems, payloads, and missile systems
Review test plans and test reports for radiation testing of electronic components against requirements on total dose, displacement damage, prompt dose rate latchup/ upset, and single event effects
Prepare survivability analysis for space environments such as micrometeoroids, atomic oxygen, solar energetic particles, and single event effects
Evaluate plans and procedures for component and box-level Flash X-ray testing
Calculate radiation environment estimations using DTRA M&S tools (ASSIST, QPROMPT, DGBETS, GSCENARIO, PRPSIM, FAB4DA, EMREP, GAP-RF), testable hardware toolkit (THTk), FASTRAD, MCNP, SPENVIS, CREME96, GEANT4, Ansys Charge Plus, SIRE2, Warren and other radiation analysis tools
Participate at program PDRs, CDRs, and other reviews as required in reviewing radiation requirements and compliance
Promote engagement with and across industry and government to review survivability/ radiation plans and implement best practices

Minimum Requirements

What You Need to be Successful

Masters degree or higher in physics, nuclear engineering, electrical engineering or other related degree
10 or more years of related post-grad experience
Experience in electron/ proton/ x-ray transport analysis or related experience
Track record reviewing NH&S analyses and NH&S requirements compliance
Proven proficiency evaluating SGEMP as a design consideration of flight hardware or related experience
Documented capability of leading evaluation of electronic components for space flight units
Demonstrated thorough understanding of prompt dose effects
Willingness to travel domestically to support customer engagements, up to 25%
This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the US government. U.S citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

Doctoral degree in physics, nuclear engineering, electrical engineer or other related degree
At least 15 years in Nuclear Hardness and Survivability
Demonstrated capability of performing radiation predictions using DTRA ASSIST, THTk, FAB4DA, FASTRAD, MCNP, GEANT4, Ansys Software Suite, SPENVIS, CREME96, ICEPIC and other radiation tools
Extensive expertise of radiation effects and interactions on electric components and materials
Deep experience planning, executing, and analyzing radiation test programs for parts against relevant radiation environments
Proven systems engineering experience with ability to apply to survivability questions
Participate in industry and government forums in the space community, including SPWG, JEDEC/SAE, HEART and IEEE groups
Active TS/SCI or Q clearance

Job Description

This Laboratory Technician role focuses on providing analytical support for gas and hydrocarbon liquid testing while strictly adhering to established quality, safety, environmental, and laboratory procedures. Responsibilities

Receive and log samples accurately into the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS).
Perform analytical testing on gas and hydrocarbon liquid samples using Gas Chromatography (GC), RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation methods.
Follow standardized testing methods, including SOPs, GPA methods, and other approved analytical protocols to ensure data integrity and consistency.
Generate, review, and report test results to customers, and communicate findings clearly via phone and email as needed.
Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of laboratory instruments and equipment to maintain optimal performance.
Assist with cylinder cleaning, preparation, and shipping to support laboratory operations and sample handling workflows.
Perform general laboratory housekeeping to maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.
Follow all laboratory safety, quality, environmental, and ethics procedures at all times.
Maintain thorough documentation and recordkeeping for all tests, results, and laboratory activities in accordance with quality management system (QMS) requirements.

Essential Skills

Associates or Bachelors degree in Chemistry, Biology, Physical Science, or a closely related field.
Minimum of 2 years of laboratory experience in an analytical or testing environment.
Experience working with Gas Chromatography (GC) in a laboratory setting.
Proven ability to follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and standardized test methods.
Strong documentation and recordkeeping skills, including accurate data entry into LIMS and other systems.
Ability to work comfortably and efficiently in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Experience performing analytical testing such as RVP, molecular weight, density, and distillation.

Experience in hydrocarbon, petroleum, chemical, energy, environmental, or testing laboratory settings.
Experience using LIMS systems for sample tracking and data management.

Background in life science or analytical testing disciplines.

Job Title: Quality Control Technician II
Job Description

The Quality Control Technician II plays a key role in ensuring that food products consistently meet internal quality expectations and regulatory food safety standards. This position focuses on routine monitoring, inspections, and data collection across production lines, helping to maintain a safe and compliant operation while supporting continuous improvement in quality assurance and quality control.

Perform product temperature checks throughout production to verify compliance with food safety and quality specifications.
Conduct ATP equipment hygiene checks to confirm proper sanitation and cleanliness of production equipment.
Inspect equipment for cleanliness and sanitation readiness before and during use.
Perform Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspections on the production floor to ensure adherence to established standards.
Conduct sanitizer concentration verification to confirm proper dosing and effectiveness.
Measure pH and salt concentrations to ensure products meet defined quality parameters.
Perform detailed pre-operational inspections prior to production start-up to verify that all equipment and areas are ready for use.
Verify water temperatures used in production and sanitation processes to ensure compliance with established requirements.
Accurately document all inspection and test results in the appropriate systems or logs.
Report any deviations, non-conformances, or potential food safety risks promptly to quality assurance leadership.

Hands-on experience in the meat industry, with familiarity with production processes and food safety considerations.
Strong understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and the ability to perform GMP inspections.
Experience performing temperature checks on products and process equipment in a production environment.
Ability to conduct weight checks and basic calibration-related activities for production and quality equipment.
Experience in quality assurance and quality control within a food manufacturing setting.
Ability to perform and interpret pH readings and salt concentration measurements.
Proficiency with basic computer skills for data entry, documentation, and reporting of quality results.

Comfort working in both hot and cold environments, including refrigerated and freezer areas.
Ability to work flexible shifts, including early morning or daytime schedules, as assigned.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer
jobs.description:
Mechanical Engineering AI Trainer

Role Overview

Engagement: Fully remote, project-based AI training work

Hours: At least ~10h/week, no weekly maximum; full-time hours are available

Pay: $40-$125 per hour USD, paid via PayPal

Location: United States, Canada, or the UK

First step: Skills assessment: about 2-4 hours, unpaid

About the Role

A leading AI Lab is looking for experienced mechanical engineers to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real engineering work: sizing a component against a real load case, reading a CAD assembly and spotting what interferes at full travel, a tolerance stack up, a thermal or fluids calculation, a DFM decision, a failure analysis.

The models can already talk fluently about mechanical engineering; what they cannot yet do reliably is the actual work. You bring the judgment you have built catching the failure mode the spec sheet does not mention. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.
In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a component sizing calculation with a worked solution, a tolerance stack up, a CAD assembly review with interference and clearance findings, a thermal or fluids analysis, a DFM and DFA review, a failure analysis report, or a test and validation plan, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional mechanical engineering role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long form and self directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Responsibilities

Design challenging, realistic mechanical engineering tasks drawn from your own day to day work: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files an engineer would need (drawings, CAD models, load cases, material data, test data, specifications), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the calculation, design review, analysis or report) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write closed ended problems with worked solutions and acceptance criteria, and detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain, such as the right loads and factors, the right material, the right tolerances and the right failure modes considered, and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: wrong boundary conditions, unit errors, interferences missed, tolerance stacks that do not close, unsafe factors of safety, fabricated or ignored source files, and off brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across design, analysis, manufacturing and test, and review and refine tasks built by other engineers.

Domain Qualifications

2+ years of professional mechanical engineering experience preferred. Any specialty: design and product development, manufacturing, thermal, structural, automotive, aerospace, HVAC, robotics, energy, medical devices.
In progress Bachelor’s degree or higher in mechanical engineering or a related field. PE licensure is a plus but not required.
Depth in at least one of: mechanical design and CAD (geometry, clearances, tolerances, mechanisms); structures and materials (stress, deflection, fatigue, buckling, material selection, failure analysis); thermal and fluids (heat transfer, thermodynamics, HVAC, pumps and piping); dynamics and controls (vibration, kinematics, rotating machinery); manufacturing (DFM and DFA, process selection, GD&T, tolerance stack ups, cost and quality trade offs).
Fluency in the tools of your specialty: CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, Creo, NX, CATIA or Inventor), FEA or CFD, or MATLAB or Python for engineering analysis.
Strong fundamentals across mechanics of materials, dynamics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics and manufacturing processes.
Meticulous: you check your own work and enjoy finding the edge case that breaks an assumption.

General Requirements

2+ years of hands on experience in your field preferred (see Domain qualifications above). Candidates with less experience are considered where the practical work is real.
Able to draw on your own real world experience and day to day workflows to craft scenarios that test whether an AI system can actually do the work.
Hands on practitioner: you currently do (or recently did) the work yourself at an individual contributor level, not solely in a managerial capacity.
Full professional or native level written and spoken English, with strong written communication. You can explain complex professional reasoning clearly and concisely, and articulate why a result is wrong, not only that it is.
Comfort with ambiguity and attention to detail. You can orient in a new set of files and build an accurate, deep working picture of it quickly, especially when the subject sits partly outside your own specialization. You verify what a document claims against the underlying numbers, sources or facts.
Capable of interpreting feedback, judging which parts of it are actually correct, and applying it without hand holding. When stuck, you look for the answer rather than waiting for one.
Ability to ramp quickly on unfamiliar work from written material and instructions alone, including where that material is incomplete (for example, writing grading rubrics for the first time).
General familiarity with AI and LLM tools. You have used models like Claude or ChatGPT in professional work and have the judgment to tell a well reasoned answer from a plausible sounding but incorrect one.
Baseline tech literacy: comfortable with cloud file tools (e.g., Google Workspace), managing browser profiles, downloading and installing desktop apps (e.g., Claude), and everyday file handling (e.g., converting between Excel and Google Sheets, zipping files for sharing).
Available at least 10 hours per week, with no weekly maximum. Consistent availability is valued and full time hours are available.
Based in the United States, Canada, or the UK.

Compensation and Terms

Pay: $40-$125/hr USD. Paid via PayPal on a regular cadence.
Contract position. Fully remote. Minimum 10 hours per week with no weekly maximum.
Flexible scheduling. Multi day task timers let you spread work across days.
Access to Claude and ChatGPT is provided through the project; no personal subscription is required.

What to Expect

Apply through your agency link and create your account.
Complete the skills assessment (about 2 to 4 hours, unpaid). It tests domain fit, careful reading, and how you judge a model's output against a professional standard. All work must be your own; submissions produced with AI tools are rejected, and this is the single most common reason candidates do not pass.
Our team reviews your assessment. If you pass, you complete onboarding, start on regular paid projects in your field, and complete a short training project that walks through how tasks, files, and rubrics are built.
Propose a task from your professional experience: the scenario, the prompt, the files you will build, and where you expect the model to fail. An expert reviewer reads it and sends written feedback either way.
Once your proposal is accepted, build the task in full and run it against frontier models. Every completed task goes through expert review, and experienced contributors are invited to review and refine other experts' tasks.
Each stage is a gate: work must be accepted before you move on. You are compensated for every step you complete, but not every submission is accepted. Feedback and revision are a normal part of the process. Support is available through platform instructions, onboarding materials, a dedicated Slack channel, and office hours.

About Artiva:

Artiva is clinical-stage, publicly-traded biotechnology company focused on developing natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies for patients suffering from devastating autoimmune diseases and cancers. Artiva’s lead program, AlloNK®, is an allogeneic, off-the-shelf, non-genetically modified NK cell therapy candidate designed to enhance the antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity effect of monoclonal antibodies to drive B-cell depletion. AlloNK is delivered in the outpatient setting with no required hospitalization.

AlloNK is currently being evaluated in three ongoing clinical trials for the treatment of B-cell driven autoimmune diseases. This includes two company-sponsored trials, one in systemic lupus erythematosus for patients with or without lupus nephritis, and a basket trial across autoimmune diseases (Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Sclerosis, Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies and Sjögren’s Disease), as well as an investigator-initiated basket trial in B-cell driven autoimmune diseases. Artiva’s pipeline also includes CAR-NK candidates targeting both solid and hematologic cancers.

Artiva was founded in 2019 as a spin out of GC Cell, formerly GC Lab Cell Corporation, a leading healthcare company in the Republic of Korea, pursuant to a strategic partnership granting Artiva exclusive worldwide rights (excluding Asia, Australia and New Zealand) to GC Cell’s NK cell manufacturing technology and programs. Artiva is headquartered in San Diego, California.

jobs.description:
Maxonic maintains a close and long-term relationship with our direct client. In support of their needs, we are looking for a Research Associate - II.

Job Description

Job Title:
Research Associate - II

Job Type: Contract

Job Location: Oceanside, CA

Work Schedule: Onsite

Pay Rate: $56, Based on experience

Description

We are seeking a highly motivated Associate Scientist to support purification process development during pivotal and commercial development phases. This contract role focuses on high‑throughput purification of upstream/cell culture samples and supports downstream purification characterization studies. A core part of this role is the development and optimization of high‑throughput purification assays using state‑of‑the‑art automation platforms (e.g., Tecan, Hamilton).

The ideal candidate brings strong hands‑on laboratory skills, deep familiarity with HTP purification methods, and the ability to establish, troubleshoot, and refine automated workflows.

Key Responsibilities

High‑Throughput Purification & Automation
Execute high‑throughput purification (HTP) workflows for upstream/cell culture samples to support process characterization.
Operate, optimize, and maintain automated liquid handling systems such as Hamilton and Tecan platforms.
Develop, qualify, and refine HTP purification assays and microscale purification methods.
Collaborate with upstream teams to ensure timely sample processing and data delivery.
Purification Process Development
Contribute to experimental design and execute purification process development and characterization experiments.
Conduct bench‑scale purification studies using chromatography, filtration, and microscale systems.
Collect, analyze, and interpret experimental data in compliance with data integrity expectations.
Prepare high‑quality protocols, reports, and electronic laboratory notebook documentation.
Technical Excellence & Collaboration
Support implementation of new purification technologies, instrumentation, and platform enhancements.
Maintain a state‑of‑the‑art purification lab, including instrumentation readiness and workflow improvements.
Partner with upstream, downstream, and cross‑functional colleagues as needed on development and characterization initiatives.
Follow all compliance, training, and safety requirements.

Qualifications / Skills / Experience

M.S. with 2+ years or B.S. with 4+ years of relevant industry experience in chemical engineering, biochemistry, bioengineering, or related discipline.
Expertise developing and executing HTP purification assays, including automated liquid handling systems such as Tecan, Hamilton, and microscale chromatography platforms.
Experience with chromatography (e.g., AKTA, plate‑based), filtration, and standard downstream techniques.
Strong analytical, documentation, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work both independently and in collaborative, fast‑paced environments.
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.

About Maxonic

Since 2002 Maxonic has been at the forefront of connecting candidate strengths to client challenges. Our award winning, dedicated team of recruiting professionals are specialized by technology, are great listeners, and will seek to find a position that meets the long-term career needs of our candidates. We take pride in the over 10,000 candidates that we have placed, and the repeat business that we earn from our satisfied clients.

Interested in Applying?

Please apply with your most current resume. Feel free to contact Jaspreet Singh (Jaspreet.s@maxonic.com/(510) 613-4990) for more details.

jobs.title: Remote Python Engineer
jobs.description:
About Turing:

Turing is one of the world's leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

About the Role:

We're looking for a high-taste engineer with a strong eye for quality — someone who's worked hands-on with preference data and rubric creation, and knows what separates a good example from a great one. You communicate clearly and can synthesize complex technical work the way a strong MAI dev would: concise, structured, and easy for others to act on. You're comfortable in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and default to shipping over deliberating.

What does day-to-day look like:

Design, refine, and iterate on rubrics and evaluation criteria for preference data
Review and label data with a high bar for quality, catching subtle issues others might miss
Build and maintain pipelines/infra that support data generation, collection, and evaluation workflows
Synthesize findings from data work into clear write-ups, updates, or recommendations for the team
Collaborate closely with researchers/engineers to translate qualitative judgment into scalable processes

Required Skills:

Proficiency in Python (especially building/maintaining pipelines and infra) or Typescript (experience contributing to or navigating large codebases like VSCode a plus)
Hands-on experience with preference data collection and/or rubric creation
Strong written and verbal communication — able to distill technical work into clear, actionable summaries
Demonstrated high-taste judgment — able to articulate why something is good, not just that it is.

Perks of Freelancing With Turing:

Work in a fully remote environment.
Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI projects with leading LLM companies.

Engagement Details:

Compensation:
Market rate. Please share a specific rate expectation (rather than a range) so we can quickly assess mutual fit
Availability:
40 hours/week preferred, with a minimum 6-hour overlap with Pacific Time. If you're unable to commit to 40 hours, please share your available hours and overlap window
Employment Type: Independent contractor (does not include medical or paid leave benefits
Duration:
3 months, with an expected start date as soon as possible

Evaluation Process (approximately 30 mins):

One round of interview (30 mins of technical & cultural discussion)

jobs.title: Research Associate
jobs.description:
Corteva Agriscience is seeking a hands-on Research Associate
to help build field research capabilities at a growing agricultural research center in the Indianapolis area. In this role, you will join the Integrated Field Science team and support high-quality, multi-crop field research from trial setup through harvest and closeout. You will work alongside scientists, agronomy colleagues, and technical partners to execute research protocols, maintain research plots, collect reliable data, and keep field operations running safely and efficiently. Working with minimal guidance, you will also conduct experiments and complex technical activities, interpret results, refine methodologies, and recommend practical next steps. This is an opportunity to apply your agricultural experience and scientific judgment while helping shape the capabilities and culture of a highly visible research center.

What You'll Do

Help plan and conduct field research trials, including site preparation, planting, treatment application, crop maintenance, sampling, assessment, harvest, and trial closeout.
Working with minimal guidance, conduct experiments, complex technical operations, and information-search or analysis projects.
Optimize, interpret, and independently adapt methodologies for current projects; recommend additional experiments or alternative approaches when appropriate.
Recognize erroneous or unexpected results, analyze and interpret findings, draw sound conclusions, and recommend a path forward.
Contribute to work plans and manage daily workflow to deliver accurate, timely research results.
Execute research protocols accurately and collect, record, quality-check, and organize field data for use in project summaries and reports.
Operate, transport, maintain, and help troubleshoot agricultural and research equipment used for application, planting, harvesting, sensing, and data collection.
Coordinate day-to-day field activities with scientists, agronomy colleagues, seasonal employees, interns, contractors, and technical partners across on-site and off-site research locations.
Promote strong standards for safety, stewardship, compliance, data integrity, equipment care, and continuous improvement.
Support field demonstrations, tours, and other activities that connect agricultural research with customers, partners, and visitors.

Why This Role Matters

The Indianapolis-area research center is being developed as a hub for agricultural research, innovation, learning, and internal and external engagement. Your work will help establish dependable field research capabilities and create an environment where scientific concepts can be evaluated under practical agricultural conditions and showcased to internal and external groups.

What Skills You Need

A Bachelor's degree in Agronomy, Crop Science, Plant Science, Weed Science, Plant Pathology, Entomology, Agricultural Engineering, or a related discipline; or at least five years of directly related agricultural research experience.
Experience conducting applied agricultural field trials and completing field activities such as planting, treatment application, crop maintenance, assessment, sampling, and harvest.
Demonstrated ability to work with minimal guidance, analyze experimental results, identify unexpected outcomes, and make evidence-based recommendations.
Experience operating and calibrating agricultural equipment, with the mechanical aptitude to perform routine setup, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
A valid driver's license and the ability to work safely in outdoor agricultural conditions, including seasonal work demands.
Indiana Commercial Applicator License, Category 10 Research and Demonstration at minimum, or the ability to obtain it as soon as possible.
Authorization to work in the United States.

Preferred Skills

Experience with multi-crop research, crop protection, biological products, or agricultural technology platforms.
Experience using digital field-research tools, research data systems, sensors, drones, or precision agriculture technologies.
Working knowledge of experimental protocols, data-quality practices, pesticide stewardship, or regulated field-research requirements.
Experience independently adapting research methods or technical procedures to meet project needs.
Experience coordinating seasonal employees, interns, contractors, or work crews.
Experience supporting field demonstrations, tours, or other stakeholder-engagement activities.

What You'll Gain

Opportunities to strengthen your scientific, technical, operational, and leadership capabilities.
Collaboration with scientists, innovators, and agricultural professionals.
The opportunity to help build a growing research center and contribute to agricultural solutions with real-world impact.

Benefits - How We'll Support You

Numerous development opportunities offered to build your skills
Be part of a company with a higher purpose and contribute to making the world a better place
Health benefits for you and your family on your first day of employment
Four weeks of paid time off and two weeks of well-being pay per year, plus paid holidays
Excellent parental leave which includes a minimum of 16 weeks for mother and father
Future planning with our competitive retirement savings plan and tuition reimbursement program
Learn more about our total rewards package here - Corteva Benefits
Check out life at Corteva! www.linkedin.com/company/corteva/life

Are you a good match? Apply today! We seek applicants from all backgrounds to ensure we get the best, most creative talent on our team.

Corteva Agriscience is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to embracing our differences to enrich lives, advance innovation, and boost company performance. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, military or veteran status, pregnancy related conditions (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), disability or any other protected status in accordance with federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Logistics Data Analyst - Clearance Required
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Logistics Data Analyst – Clearance Required based in the United States.

This role offers the opportunity to apply data analytics and logistics expertise to support critical federal preparedness and radiological and nuclear detection programs. You will transform complex datasets into reliable insights that improve reporting, resource allocation, and mission execution. Working with federal agencies and program stakeholders, you will help maintain accurate data, optimize analytical processes, and strengthen program management activities. The position combines advanced Excel analysis, process improvement, documentation, and support for grant and program execution. Success requires a highly organized, detail-oriented professional who takes initiative and thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. This is a remote-capable position supporting a federal mission and requires an active Secret security clearance, along with the ability to obtain DHS Suitability.

Accountabilities

As a Logistics Data Analyst, you will deliver accurate, actionable analytical products while supporting program operations, process improvement, and government reporting requirements. You will collaborate with federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial stakeholders to strengthen radiological and nuclear detection capabilities and improve operational efficiency.

Support the development, implementation, and sustainment of radiological and nuclear detection programs and capabilities across federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial agencies.
Provide information resources, processes, facilitation, and guidance for document development, strategic planning, and the creation of plans and procedures.
Create, maintain, and optimize Excel spreadsheets using advanced formulas, pivot tables, lookup functions, conditional logic, Power Query, and data modeling.
Validate, clean, standardize, and analyze datasets to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance with federal reporting requirements.
Develop analytical products and reports that help government and contractor personnel make informed decisions, allocate resources efficiently, and execute mission objectives.

jobs.title: NPI Laboratory Technician
jobs.description:
Therm-x of California is the leading manufacturer for Advanced Temperature and Control Systems for Hi-Technology industries. We have been in business for over 30 years and have a diverse customer base. We offer **competitive pay,** and a comprehensive benefits package.

We are seeking a skilled NPI Laboratory Technician to join our Engineering team. This role is focused on new product introduction (NPI) prototype workflows, RF and electrical testing, and electro-mechanical assembly within a dedicated laboratory environment. Reporting directly to the Engineering Manager, the successful candidate will support product development and validation activities, ensuring all assemblies meet customer and industry specifications. The role requires strong technical laboratory skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently within an ISO 9001 semiconductor manufacturing environment.

**Essential responsibilities and duties;**

* Read and execute work orders — including schematics, wiring diagrams, parts lists, and assembly instructions — to build, repair, and/or test electrical, electro-mechanical, vacuum, and pneumatic assemblies, subassemblies, and components.
* Perform electro-mechanical assembly operations; troubleshoot and repair units as required.
* Manage the NPI prototype area to meet customer requirements for electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance; receive and audit incoming parts, inspect for defects, and drive continuous process improvements.
* Set up, operate, and maintain RF test equipment including vector network analyzers (VNA), spectrum analyzers, signal generators, power meters, and impedance analyzers to characterize RF assemblies and components.
* Perform RF measurements including S-parameters (S11, S21, etc.), insertion loss, return loss, VSWR, impedance matching, gain/phase response, and frequency response across specified test frequencies.
* Use electronic measurement equipment — including DMMs, oscilloscopes, waveform generators, LCR meters, and lock-in amplifiers — and test fixtures, leak detectors, and vacuum pumps to verify electrical performance and test assemblies; maintain calibration records for all equipment.
* Interpret RF test data, generate test reports, and disposition units as pass/fail against acceptance criteria; escalate anomalies to engineering.
* Support development and maintenance of RF test fixtures, jigs, and automated test setups; apply RF shielding, grounding, and cable management best practices to ensure measurement integrity.
* Operate and troubleshoot laboratory equipment including 3D printers, plastic engraving/cutting lasers, and precision measurement tools (calipers, scales, gauges).
* Collaborate closely with engineers on new product development and validation; support technology transfer activities including training laboratory staff on procedures and test methods.
* Maintain laboratory organization, inventory, and equipment calibration schedules; complete all required documentation including test results, nonconformance reports, and progress records in compliance with ISO 9001 requirements.
* Interpret and apply mechanical and electrical circuit drawings, RF schematic layouts, and assembly specifications; perform software installs and equipment firmware updates as needed.

**Desired Skills;**

* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Strategic agility with strong critical and logical thinking; ability to analyze complex problems and perform functions with minimal guidance.
* Ability to prioritize, multi-task, and adapt in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
* Hands-on capability in a lab and prototype assembly setting.
* Experience coordinating and collaborating across teams to meet organizational goals.
* Experience working within an ISO 9001 quality environment.
* Ability to understand tolerances and compliance requirements within the semiconductor industry.
* Experience with precision measurement tools such as calipers and scales.
* Proficiency with electrical test equipment: DMM, oscilloscope, waveform generator, and related instruments.
* 5+ years of hands-on experience as a manufacturing technician, laboratory technician, or laboratory assistant in a semiconductor, electronics, or related technical manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience with RF test equipment (VNA, spectrum analyzer, signal generator, power meter) and RF measurement techniques.
* Proficiency with standard electronic test instruments: DMM, oscilloscope, and waveform generator.
* Experience working within an ISO 9001 quality environment.

**Physical Demands:** While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; talk or hear and taste or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.

Aethel Defense tests AI applications such as chatbots and AI agents for security weaknesses. Role overview

Osmind powers the largest network of independent psychiatry practices in the country — 1,000+ clinics — on top of our own EHR and real-world evidence platform. Our Biosciences team turns that data and clinical footprint into partnerships with biopharma companies across our four life sciences product lines: clinical real-world evidence, clinical research, commercial real-world evidence, and sales & marketing solutions. See osmind.org/life-sciences for more information.

Our Biosciences unit is a small, fast-moving team sitting at the intersection of neuropsychiatry, data, and commercial strategy — and this hire will be one of the first few people building it out. You'll have direct exposure to biopharma partners and executive leadership from your first month, and the scope of what you own will expand quickly — from contributing to workstreams, to owning them outright, to eventually shaping the direction of an engagement.

What you’ll do

Commercial modeling

Build and own commercial models detailing specific market TAMs, expected product revenues, psychiatric clinic revenue modeling, and epidemiological based forecasting
Combine clinical trial data, market research, and analyst reports into competitive landscape analyses
Build scenario-based models capable of demonstrating first and second order effects of various inputs

Research design and execution

Design, edit, program, and field quantitative surveys for a variety of clinician audiences. This includes end-to-end execution across instrument design through analysis.
Draft clinician interview guides and lead subsequent interviews
Run research operations end to end, from participant recruiting through fieldwork completion
Turn primary research and real-world evidence into insights that move a commercial project forward

Data and evidence

Analyze real-world datasets spanning claims and EHR data to find actionable insights
Design and build both prospective and retrospective data analysis projects
Track the competitive and launch landscape for the therapies our partners care about

Partnerships

This role is built for someone who will mature into a full end-to-end client lead. You will have high exposure to our partners from the start.
Build the deliverables that go to partners: presentation slide decks, handoff-ready models, conference abstracts, and more
Manage against real deadlines, including external review windows you don't control
Learn Osmind's rights-to-win well enough that you can eventually write a proposal end-to-end — scope, pricing, terms — for a new business opportunity. Sit in client and prospect meetings, help write proposals, support negotiations, and support project execution & upsell discussions.
Leverage your client-facing abilities to develop deep relationships, effectively project manage client projects, and identify and execute on cross-sell and upsell opportunities
Maintain an understanding of R&D pipelines, M&A activity, funding activity, asset development, etc. of neuropsychiatry drug and device development

Requirements

At least 2 years at a life sciences consulting firm (or within a commercial analytics, market research, business operations role within a biotech company)
Direct commercial biopharma exposure across product forecasting, launch/GTM strategy, market access, and payer dynamics
Advanced Excel skills: You've built complex models from scratch and owned them end to end. Comfortable with scenario logic, sensitivity analysis, and structuring a model someone else can pick up
Survey instrument design experience (Qualtrics, Typeform, or similar platforms)
Capable of translating both unstructured and structured data into actionable analyses and insights that solve our clients questions
Attention to detail and operational excellence
Comfort with ambiguity, and the initiative to move a deliverable forward without being told to
This role is based in San Francisco and has an in-office requirement of twice a week

Advanced analytics experience (Python, R, SQL)
Psychiatry, neuroscience, or CNS experience
Startup experience or small-team background
A degree in a relevant scientific field (neuroscience, biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, biostatistics, etc.)

About The Company

Oracle is a global technology leader renowned for its innovative cloud solutions, enterprise software, and hardware systems. With a rich history spanning several decades, Oracle empowers organizations across various industries to achieve digital transformation through its comprehensive suite of products and services. Committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace, Oracle continuously invests in cutting-edge technologies and talent development to drive business success and societal impact worldwide.

About The Role

The Principal HR Data Analyst at Oracle is a strategic role that involves leveraging advanced analytics, data science, and workforce insights to support HR leadership and business decision-making processes. This position requires a highly analytical mindset, strong technical skills, and the ability to translate complex workforce data into clear, actionable insights. The role is collaborative, working closely with HR Business Partners (HRBPs), HR leaders, and other stakeholders to address critical talent and workforce challenges. The Principal HR Data Analyst will develop predictive models, scenario analyses, and forecasts that influence strategic initiatives such as workforce planning, compensation strategies, attrition management, and talent acquisition.

In this position, you will be responsible for transforming large datasets from multiple sources into meaningful visualizations and reports, applying sophisticated analytical techniques, and exploring emerging technologies like AI and machine learning to enhance HR analytics capabilities. The role demands independent problem-solving, proactive engagement with business stakeholders, and a deep understanding of workforce dynamics to anticipate trends and recommend data-driven solutions. Success in this role will enable Oracle to optimize its talent strategies and maintain a competitive edge in the industry.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will possess an advanced degree in Data Science, Statistics, Data Management, Economics, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or a related quantitative field. They should have at least 8 years of experience in people analytics, workforce planning, or a related analytical discipline. Demonstrated expertise in statistical modeling, forecasting, predictive analytics, and scenario analysis is essential. Experience applying AI, machine learning, or generative AI to business workflows is highly desirable.

Candidates should have a proven track record analyzing compensation, workforce costs, hiring, attrition, and other financial metrics related to human resources. Proficiency with Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM, OTBI, BI Publisher, and Oracle Analytics Cloud is required. Strong technical skills in SQL, Python, R, advanced Excel, and statistical techniques are necessary to identify trends, evaluate drivers, and automate analyses. Excellent communication skills are vital for synthesizing complex insights into clear narratives and visualizations tailored for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Responsibilities

Partner with HR and business leadership to define and address complex workforce questions, designing analyses across compensation, hiring, attrition, internal mobility, and workforce costs to inform strategic decisions.
Create scenario models, forecasts, and advanced analyses to quantify the impact of talent decisions on financial outcomes, including salary, equity, and other workforce-related expenses.
Gather, integrate, and synthesize HR data from various sources, transforming extensive datasets into scalable analytical models, actionable insights, and compelling data visualizations.
Serve as a subject matter expert on people data, analytical methodologies, and tools, providing guidance to stakeholders on metrics, approaches, and best practices for workforce analysis.
Utilize advanced analytical and technical skills—including SQL, Python, R, and Oracle analytics tools—to detect trends, evaluate drivers, automate processes, and generate predictive insights.
Explore and implement emerging analytical techniques such as AI and machine learning, ensuring responsible data governance, validation, and ethical use of employee data.
Exercise sound judgment in handling sensitive employee data, adhering strictly to data privacy, security, and governance standards.
Manage multiple priorities independently in a fast-paced, agile environment, demonstrating ownership, attention to detail, and accountability.
Proactively identify emerging workforce trends, risks, and opportunities, consulting with HRBPs and leaders to recommend innovative, data-driven solutions.
Communicate complex analyses effectively through executive-ready reports, presentations, and visualizations that highlight business implications and strategic recommendations.

The package includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, with access to expert medical opinions. Employees are covered under short-term and long-term disability plans, as well as life insurance and accidental death & dismemberment (AD&D) coverage. Supplemental life insurance options are available for employees, spouses, and children.

Additional benefits include healthcare and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts, pre-tax commuter and parking benefits, and a 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company matching contributions. Paid time off includes flexible vacation policies, accrued based on tenure and work hours, along with 11 paid holidays annually. New hires receive paid sick leave, which can be carried over up to a maximum cap. Parental leave, adoption assistance, employee stock purchase plans, financial planning services, and group legal benefits are also provided. Voluntary benefits such as auto, homeowner, and pet insurance are available to enhance employee coverage and security.

Equal Opportunity

jobs.description:
Staff Research Associate 2 (9612C), Molecular & Cell Biology - #89397 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Molecular and Cell Biology at UC Berkeley is recognized nationally and internationally for excellence. The teaching and research activities of the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) concern the molecular structures and processes of cellular life and their roles in the function, reproduction, and development of living organisms. The types of living organisms from which the departmental faculty draws its working materials range from viruses and microbes through plants, roundworms, annelids, arthropods, and mollusks to fish, amphibia, and mammals.
  
  
The Hockemeyer Lab work to establish reliable models of human diseases using genetically engineered human and stem cell and mouse models and functional genomics screening approaches. We are particularly interested in developing rigorous genetic approaches to study human disease, development and cell biology where conventional animal models or tissue culture systems do not adequately recapitulate human biology.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
This Staff Research Associate 2 provides a variety of support and research functions within the lab for a 2-year project. This position assists lab members with molecular biology and tissue culture techniques, including the culture and maintenance of pluripotent stem cell cultures (hPSCs). The Staff Research Associate 2 supports a large-scale hPSCs genome engineering workflow involving genome editing, project tracking, and quality control. Additionally, this position works on various research projects involving the planning, design, and conduct of experiments under the supervision of the PI, while assisting with general lab operations, safety compliance, and supply management.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
**The First Review Date for this job is:** October 23, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
Stem Cell Culture and Genome Engineering - 30%
  
  
Cultures and maintains the pluripotent stem cell cultures (hPSCs) which includes the passaging of stem cell clones, isolation of genomic DNA and genotyping cells by PCR and sequencing. Support a large-scale hPSCs genome engineering workflow that involves genome editing, project tracking, quality control of reagents and materials, and report writing.
  
  
Molecular Biology and Tissue Culture Support - 25%
  
  
Standard molecular biology and tissue culture techniques. Assists lab members with the maintenance and characterization of human stem cell cultures and genotyping of stem cells which entails the isolation of DNA from human stem cells, amplifying DNA by PCR and preparing samples for sequence analysis. This genotyping will require daily record keeping in laboratory notebook to record the samples analyzed and the attendance at weekly lab meetings to understand the basic objectives of the research project.
  
  
Research Project Support - 25%
  
  
Assists with research projects including optimizing and testing tissue culture and molecular biology protocols such as molecular cloning, stem cell differentiation and library screening. This will be done with the guidance of the PI and other lab members.
  
Plans and designs the experiments discussing the outline of the experiment/ protocol with the PI, conducting the experiments, analyzing results and interpreting data under the supervision of the PI. Troubleshoots experiments which include PCR and genotyping.
  
  
Safety and Protocol Compliance - 10%
  
  
Assisting with protocol renewals and safety inspections.
  
  
Lab Support Operations - 10%
  
  
Lab support duties including autoclaving waste and ordering and restocking supplies.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Experience with sterile tissue culture techniques, PCR, basic lab maintenance duties, excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  
Experience with molecular biology techniques, plasmid handling and molecular cloning.
  
Experience with human pluripotent stem cell culturing, genome engineering with CRISPR, as well as the library prep and data analysis of next generation sequencing (NGS).
  
Knowledge of lab safety procedures, capability to design and conduct experiments and analyze data.
  
  
Preferred Qualifications
  
  
Master's degree in the life sciences, preferably Biology, Molecular and Cell Biology, Biochemistry. (Preferred)
  
  
Education / Training
  
  
Bachelor's degree in the life sciences, preferably Biology, Molecular and Cell Biology, Biochemistry.
  
1-year (cumulative) experience working in a biology research lab.

jobs.title: Lab Assistant
jobs.description:
Founded in 2016, Infinite Chemical Analysis Labs’ mission is to provide the cannabis industry with accurate and timely analytical services of exceptional quality while exceeding clients’ expectations. The lab offers a wide range of analytical services for quality assurance and state compliance to uphold brands to the highest standards for premium products. ICAL prides itself on setting the standard for quality cannabis testing across California, Michigan, and New York. Additionally, ICAL is expanding its analytical services to the fields of environmental, water, food, beverage, nutraceutical, and agriculture testing. We’ll strive to set the same standard of excellence we’re known for across the entire analytical testing industry.

We are currently seeking a **Lab Assistant** to join our California team! Lab Assistants help our Technicians and Analysts with various prepping procedures for all samples we receive in the lab for analysis in addition to routine laboratory upkeep. ***This employee will join our morning shift working Monday to Friday, 6:00pm -2:30pm.*** This position is our entry level role within our lab that does not require a college degree and is a great place to begin building a career within a growing company in an ever expansive industry.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Learn and execute ICAL's established SOPs for sample homogenization of cannabis and hemp products for testing and analysis.
* Assists with sample homogenization of environmental samples for analytical testing.
* Regular use & maintenance of: Analytical Balance, pH Meter, Moisture Balance, Water Activity Meter, Pipettes, Analytical Syringe, Cryogrinder, Industrial Blender, etc.
* Dispose of analyzed samples and follow proper chemical waste procedures.
* Ensures exceptional GMP and ISO accredited laboratory practices.
* Ensure lab safety and that personal protective equipment (PPE) is worn at all times.
* Assist with inventory of samples, consumables, and packaging.
* Records raw data accurately in the laboratory information management system (LIMs)
* Personal drive and commitment to upkeep and improvement of Client Satisfaction at ICAL.
* Performs other lab-related projects and research tasks as assigned when applicable.

**REQUIRED EDUCATION, QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

* Ideal candidate will be a creative, analytical problem-solver who can cooperatively and effectively work with colleagues.
* Understands and follows verbal and written instructions; works independently in the absence of supervision.
* Able to work quickly, without error in a high-pressure environment with ever-changing deadlines.
* Willingness to learn and grow in the analytical chemistry or microbial field.
* Effective communication skills (both verbal and written) with excellent computer, typing, and organizational abilities.
* Ability and willingness to multi-task, and the ability to prioritize and manage assignments.
* Positive attitude and willingness to work in a collaborative environment, must be a team player!
* Personal integrity, disciplined work ethic, organization skills, and motivation to work with a sense of urgency.
* Working knowledge of a broad range of plant medicine products, processes, and cultivation preferred (e.g. Cannabis, Hemp, or CBD)
* Previous experience working in a commercial laboratory/industrial environment and/or in the cannabis industry is a plus.
* Proficiency with either Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets strongly preferred.
* **Must be comfortable working with and around cannabis and hemp products.**
* **Must possess at least a High School Diploma or equivalent; Associate's or Technical/Vocational Degree a plus.**
* **In-person position; must currently reside in the San Diego, CA region.**
* **At least 1 year experience in a manufacturing, warehouse, and/or laboratory environment required.**

* 100% Employer Covered Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance

Position Summary

The Senior SME, Equivalency is the program's senior technical authority for operational technology and industrial control system cybersecurity in the maritime domain. This position conducts the technical review of all equivalency requests submitted under 33 CFR Part 101 Subpart F and assists with complex waiver requests and cybersecurity plan reviews as assigned. This is a designated Key Personnel position; the Government must acknowledge any replacement in writing.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct the detailed technical review of all equivalency requests, evaluating whether the request clearly identifies the regulatory requirement at issue, describes the proposed alternative safeguard, and provides sufficient supporting evidence for Government evaluation.
Determine whether the proposed alternative provides a level of security that meets or exceeds the effectiveness of the specified regulatory requirement, and document that analysis so it is technically supportable and traceable.
Apply Government-furnished methodologies, checklists, process guides, and decision matrices to produce preliminary recommendations of Approve, Approve with Conditions, or Deny.
Prepare consolidated review packages for the USCG representative, including the complete request with supporting documentation, the fully annotated checklist with scoring, and a draft technical analysis.
Draft signature-ready correspondence addressed to submitters for USCG review and signature, including supporting justification and any proposed conditions for Government consideration.
Assist with complex and novel waiver requests and cybersecurity plan technical reviews as assigned by the Project Manager and Sub-Project Managers.
Serve as the senior technical escalation point for OT and ICS questions raised by both review teams.
Perform quality control to ensure findings are clearly stated, technically supportable, internally consistent, and traceable to the applicable regulatory requirement or checklist element.
Support development and delivery of internal maritime and OT cybersecurity training for review personnel.
Recommend improvements to review processes, checklists, and templates for Government consideration, without establishing approval criteria or adjudication standards independent of the Government.

Required Qualifications

Seven (7) years of hands-on experience focused on OT/ICS cybersecurity.
Expert-level knowledge applying cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST CSF and ISA/IEC 62443 specifically to OT/ICS environments.
Expert-level understanding of OT network architecture and security controls, with demonstrated capability applying that knowledge to maritime systems such as vessel navigation systems, cargo handling systems, and facility automation.
At least one cybersecurity certification satisfying the certification requirement for the DoD 8140 DCWF work role of Security Control Assessor (for example CISSP, CISA, or CISM)
At least one advanced OT-focused cybersecurity certification, such as the Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional (GICSP).
Must disclose, for organizational conflict of interest screening, any current or prior engagement performed for MTSA-regulated vessel, facility, or Outer Continental Shelf facility owners or operators involving cybersecurity plan development, cybersecurity assessment, or related advisory services.

Preferred Qualifications

Additional OT and ICS certifications such as GRID, GCIP, or ISA/IEC 62443 credentials.
Prior U.S. Coast Guard, DHS, or MTSA regulatory experience.
Experience with Alternative Security Programs (ASPs) in the maritime sector.
Experience serving as an independent assessor or auditor against a published control set or checklist.
Experience authoring technical justifications or equivalency determinations for a regulator.

Technical Skills

OT and ICS network architecture, segmentation, and security control design.
Industrial and maritime protocols, including Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, NMEA 0183/2000.
Maritime systems including ECDIS, AIS, GNSS, cargo and ballast control, terminal operating systems, and crane and facility automation.
NIST Cybersecurity Framework and NIST SP 800-series risk management guidance.
ISA/IEC 62443 series.

Education

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, cybersecurity, or a related technical field preferred. Equivalent hands-on OT/ICS experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

jobs.title: Data Analyst - 176046
jobs.description:
Zachary Piper Solutions is seeking a Data Analyst (Healthcare Fraud)
to support the DVA VHA in establishing and operating a high-visibility Fraud Rapid Response Center. This mission-driven initiative focuses on accelerating the detection of healthcare fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) to protect Veterans and safeguard taxpayer dollars. The Data Analyst
will support the War Room’s analytics team by analyzing federal healthcare data, developing fraud detection rules, identifying suspicious billing patterns, and generating prioritized leads for government review. This role offers hands-on experience supporting a high-profile federal healthcare initiative using VA’s Palantir analytics platform.

Responsibilities of the Data Analyst (Healthcare Fraud) include:

Develop, test, and document analytical business rules and algorithm logic designed to identify healthcare fraud, waste, and abuse schemes.
Support provider risk scoring, case prioritization, and fraud detection criteria to help investigators identify high-risk providers and suspicious claims.
Support configuration, code development, deployment, and integration of data pipelines and analytics workflows within VA’s Palantir platform.
Combine claims, enrollment, and provider exclusion data to support a comprehensive Provider 360 view of community care providers.
Perform anomaly detection and network analysis to identify unusual billing patterns, relationships, and potential coordinated fraud schemes.
Execute recurring weekly analytics to generate prioritized lead lists and support War Room decision packages.
Extract, clean, transform, and analyze federal healthcare data to identify potential fraud indicators, improper payments, and overpayments.
Develop and maintain analytical workpapers documenting findings and supporting case review activities.
Back-test fraud detection rules, measure precision and positive predictive value (PPV), analyze false positives, and support quality assurance and corrective action plans.
Support federal benchmarking and align VHA data analysis methods with relevant CMS data and analytical practices.
Build dashboards, visualizations, and analytical outputs for fraud trend reporting, improper payment reduction initiatives, risk governance, and executive briefings.
Document rule specifications, acceptance criteria, data transformations, and analytical methodologies.
Support knowledge transfer and training to help VA staff independently operate and maintain War Room analytics.
Handle protected health information (PHI) and sensitive government data in accordance with HIPAA, VA privacy requirements, and applicable security procedures.

Qualifications of the Data Analyst (Healthcare Fraud) include:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Health Informatics, or a related field.
2–5 years of federal healthcare data analytics experience, such as working with Medicare, Medicaid, or VHA data.
Experience developing analytical business rules for healthcare data, fraud detection, payment integrity, or related use cases.
Strong coding skills in SQL and Python, or comparable analytical programming experience with PySpark or R.
Proficiency with analytics platforms and data workflows, including data pipelines, transformations, and dashboards.
Working knowledge of healthcare claims data, including claim types, CPT/HCPCS and ICD-10 codes, National Provider Identifiers (NPIs), provider data, and beneficiary data.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills.
Ability to pass a Tier 2 / Moderate Background Investigation (MBI) and obtain a VA Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card.
Legal eligibility to work in the United States.
Ability to handle PHI and sensitive information in accordance with HIPAA and VA privacy requirements and complete required VA TMS training.

Desired Qualifications:

Hands-on experience with Palantir Foundry or Gotham, particularly in healthcare analytics, fraud detection, or payment integrity.
Experience identifying healthcare billing anomalies, including upcoding, unbundling, duplicate billing, impossible days, or billing by excluded providers.
Familiarity with VA Community Care data, the CMS Integrated Data Repository (IDR), the HHS Office of Inspector General’s List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE), or SAM exclusion lists.
Experience with anomaly detection, machine learning, network analysis, or link analysis.
Experience back-testing analytical rules, measuring positive predictive value (PPV), and evaluating false-positive rates.
Proficiency with Power BI, Tableau, or similar data visualization and reporting tools.
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) credential or a relevant data analytics certification.

Compensation for the Data Analyst (Healthcare Fraud) includes:

Salary Range: $100,000–$110,000 depending on experience
Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) Plan, Holidays, PTO, and sick leave as required by law
Work Arrangement: 100% remote within the continental United States, with East Coast working hours & occasional travel to DC, for in-person meetings

jobs.description:
Financial Analyst — AI Model Reviewer

About The Role

What if your deep knowledge of financial modeling could directly shape how AI performs the work of a professional analyst? We're looking for Finance Subject Matter Experts who also know their way around Python and GitHub to audit, refine, and improve AI-generated financial modeling tasks — making sure they mirror how real analysts actually work.

You'll review AI task instructions and scoring rubrics, then roll up your sleeves and edit Markdown files and Python scripts directly via Pull Requests to fix logic errors, close clarity gaps, and ensure every task meets professional standards. If you can build a DCF in your sleep and know your way around a P&L, this role was made for you.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role. Candidates must have strong US-based financial knowledge and fluency with American financial terminology and conventions.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Compensation: $80–$110/hour
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Audit AI-generated financial modeling tasks to ensure they accurately replicate professional analyst workflows
Validate task instructions and scoring rubrics for logical soundness, completeness, and real-world relevance
Directly edit Markdown files and Python scripts via Pull Requests to resolve logic errors, ambiguity, or clarity gaps
Evaluate whether AI outputs reflect correct application of concepts like DCF analysis, P&L interpretation, financial statement modeling, and valuation techniques
Provide clear, structured feedback grounded in professional financial expertise
Collaborate asynchronously with a distributed team using GitHub-based workflows
Work independently on task-based assignments at your own pace and schedule

Who You Are

Deep subject matter expertise in finance — you've worked as an analyst, in investment banking, corporate finance, equity research, FP&A, or a closely related field
Strong command of US-based financial terminology and frameworks (DCF, P&L, balance sheet analysis, WACC, comparable company analysis, etc.)
Proficient in Python — comfortable reading, writing, and debugging scripts used for financial calculations
Experienced with GitHub — you can clone repos, create branches, and submit Pull Requests without hand-holding
Comfortable editing Markdown for technical documentation
Detail-oriented with a systematic, quality-driven approach to review work
Clear, precise written communicator who can articulate what's wrong and why
Self-motivated and reliable when working independently

Nice to Have

CFA, CPA, or MBA with a finance concentration
Professional experience building financial models in Excel or Python for deal evaluation, forecasting, or valuation
Background in teaching, mentoring, or creating training materials for financial concepts
Familiarity with AI/ML evaluation workflows or data annotation projects
Experience writing or reviewing technical rubrics or assessment criteria

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs

jobs.title: E11 Bio - Sample Optimization & Agentic Microscopy Scientist
jobs.description:
E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards whole brain scale for humans and other mammals. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable mammalian brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap.

E11 Bio is seeking a mission-aligned experimental scientist, equally at home at the bench, the microscope, and in quantitative data analysis, who brings an engineering approach to the full pipeline, from sample preparation through molecular readout tools and microscopy. This role involves both optimizing the physical preparation of the tissue and implementing agentic microscopy. Reporting to the Barcoding Lead, you will define what high-quality tissue means quantitatively and will drive the improvement of high quality morphology and protein readout by working closely with molecular biology, imaging, and computational teams to support whole-brain connectomics.

Responsibilities

Develop and deploy an assay to systematically evaluate and improve the fixation quality and preservation of brain tissue
Establish and integrate quantitative metrics of molecular readout e.g. protein retention, antigenicity, and labeling quality across tissue preparation conditions
Drive the development of data-analysis pipelines to routinely generate key performance indicators of sample tissue quality
Work closely with in vivo research technicians to design experiments, evaluate results, and optimize SOPs
In collaboration with external and internal partners, drive agentic control and quality control of automated microscopy to enable consistent data quality over long acquisitions
In collaboration with external and internal partners, extend agentic control beyond acquisition to the everyday steps of the sample pipeline (e.g. liquid handling, staining, gelation, and intermediate readouts)
In collaboration with external partners, source new binders, including via novel design approaches, against synaptic and barcode targets

Outcomes

In the first 6 Months

Characterized how much perfusion quality varies between brains, measured in fixed tissue, and the effect of this variability on downstream morphology outcomes
Deployed an assay or metrics that reliably allows samples to be ranked before entering a production run
Established a rubric for tissue artifacts at the M3 level, covering how the tissue and how this affects overall reconstruction ability
Recorded a measurable > 20% improvement in expanded ultrastructural image quality compared to current baseline perfusion & gelation protocol
Deployed real-time agentic control on at least one microscope and demonstrated production acquisitions with agent monitoring instead of human
External AI-driven epitope-binder collaboration launched with agreed scope

In 12 Months:

80% of samples entering gelation at E11 meet or exceed our sample quality threshold (rolling average)
If tissue artifacts affect segmentation, 80% of samples entering gelation at E11 meet or exceed our tissue quality threshold (rolling average)
Incorporated protein retention, antigenicity, and specificity as per-stage metrics across the sample generation pipeline and demonstrated their predictive power for key downstream outcomes (e.g. segmentability)
Agentic control and fault detection running across parallelized microscopes with measured increase in unattended acquisition time without loss of quality
Identified and validated multiple cocktails of binders for stratifying excitatory and inhibitory synapses

Job Title

Staff CAD/EDA Tools Engineer

About Cognichip

At Cognichip, we are building AI-native tools that transform how semiconductor engineers create, verify, and optimize chips. Our platform combines large proprietary models, agentic workflows, domain-specific engineering intelligence, and high-performance simulation infrastructure to accelerate one of the world's most complex engineering disciplines.

About The Role

We are seeking a Staff CAD/EDA Tools Engineer to own the application layer of our EDA tool ecosystem: the wrapper scripts, CLI tooling, and container images that let engineers and AI systems run open-source and commercial chip design tools reliably and consistently. You will maintain and extend internal tooling running on the cloud at scale. If you like turning EDA tool quirks into clean, dependable software that other engineers and AI agents can build on, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain and evolve wrapper scripts and CLI tooling that give a single, consistent interface across open-source EDA tools (Verilator, Yosys, slang, Icarus Verilog, cocotb) and commercial tools.
Build, harden, and version Docker images that package EDA tools with correct dependencies and licenses, and publish them for reliable use across the team.
Own the application layer of the EDA tool stack end-to-end: evaluate and integrate new open-source tools, and write the scripts and configuration that make them usable in real design and verification flows.
Diagnose and fix tool compatibility issues, version drift, and build breakages across simulators, synthesis tools, and container environments.
Support application-layer license configuration for commercial EDA tools (e.g., FlexLM-based license servers), partnering with DevOps, who own the underlying infrastructure.
Collaborate with DevOps on how containerized tools are deployed and consumed, while owning the container image content and correctness yourself.
Partner with RTL design, verification, and AI/ML engineers to understand workflow needs and translate them into reliable, documented tooling.
Write clear documentation for tool usage, wrapper APIs, and container images so other engineers, and Cognichip's AI agents, can self-serve.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field.
10+ years of experience in software/tools engineering, and CAD/EDA infrastructure.
Hands-on experience with open-source EDA/HDL tools such as Verilator, Yosys, Icarus Verilog, or similar RTL simulation/synthesis tools.
Strong scripting and software engineering skills in Python and Bash, including building CLI tools or wrappers around third-party software.
Solid working knowledge of Docker: writing Dockerfiles, building and versioning images, and troubleshooting containerized environments.
Familiarity with digital design EDA tools from Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens
Comfortable working in Linux environments and debugging tool, build, and dependency issues independently.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with hardware verification methodologies and frameworks (UVM, or similar).
Experience with declarative build/dependency systems for hardware projects
Experience with FlexLM or other license-management systems for EDA tools.
Familiarity with cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) as a consumer of container images built for cloud deployment.
Startup or small-team experience owning a tooling area end-to-end with minimal hand-holding.

What It's Like Here

We're a fast-moving AI startup with a collaborative, high-trust culture. We value technical excellence, ownership, and the freedom to experiment. Our best work happens when our builders and innovators work closely together to turn ambitious ideas into category defining products. We operate on a hybrid schedule with four days in office, one day remote. If you're excited to build cutting edge tools that empower semiconductor engineers and reshape how chips are designed, you'll feel right at home.
