Specimen Processor (Sample Handling Assistant)

Looking to break into the laboratory field or grow your lab operations experience? Join Labcorp and play a critical role in handling specimens that directly support clinical research and patient care.

Labcorp
is seeking a detail-oriented Specimen Processor to join its bio-pharma laboratory team in Torrance, CA. This position is responsible for receiving, processing, documenting, and managing clinical trial specimens while ensuring sample integrity and compliance with quality standards. If you're dependable, organized, and thrive in a structured environment, this is a great opportunity to build a long-term career with a leading laboratory organization.

What's In It For You

Work for one of the nation's leading laboratory organizations

Contract position with potential for permanent hire

Extensive hands-on training and career development

Gain experience supporting clinical trials, pathology, and histology operations

One-step interview process

Learn valuable laboratory operations and specimen management skills

Join a collaborative and supportive team environment

Job Description

The Specimen Processor is responsible for the accurate receipt, handling, processing, and documentation of patient and clinical trial specimens before laboratory analysis. This role works with irreplaceable samples and plays a critical role in maintaining specimen integrity, supporting laboratory operations, and ensuring compliance with established quality standards and procedures.

Responsibilities

Receive and process specimen shipments from multiple couriers

Open, inspect, and properly handle incoming specimen shipments

Maintain specimen integrity and temperature requirements during processing

Scan shipments and update specimen information within internal databases

Sort and route specimens according to established procedures

Perform quality control checks on specimens, requisitions, and materials

Enter patient demographics and administrative information accurately

Image and archive requisition documents for laboratory records

Process specimen kits and perform manual aliquoting when required

Operate, maintain, and clean laboratory equipment and automation systems

Identify and resolve shipment discrepancies or misrouted specimens

Follow all SOPs, quality standards, and laboratory safety procedures

Essential Skills

High School Diploma or GED required

Minimum 1 Year Of Applicable Work Experience

Strong attention to detail and accuracy

Reliable attendance and punctuality

Ability to follow detailed procedures and instructions

Strong organizational and documentation skills

Comfortable using Microsoft Excel and Word

Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities

Ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively

Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS)

Kaiser Permanente | Harbor City Medical Center | Harbor City, CA

Are you a Clinical Laboratory Scientist who thrives on solving complex challenges, working with advanced laboratory technology, and playing a critical role in patient care? Join Kaiser Permanente
, one of California's premier healthcare organizations, and become part of a high-performing laboratory team where your expertise directly impacts patient outcomes every day.

Whether you're validating critical results, troubleshooting instrumentation, or supporting life-saving diagnoses, you'll be at the center of delivering exceptional healthcare in a fast-paced hospital environment.

Why You'll Love This Opportunity

Work with one of California's most respected healthcare systems
Gain hands-on experience with advanced laboratory instrumentation and testing platforms
Join a collaborative team of laboratory professionals, physicians, nurses, and pharmacists
Potential for contract extension and long-term opportunities
Competitive pay: $55.00 - $68.00 per hour
Make a meaningful impact on patient care through accurate and timely laboratory testing

What You'll Be Doing

As a Clinical Laboratory Scientist, you'll perform complex testing across multiple laboratory disciplines while ensuring the highest standards of quality, safety, and accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Perform complex automated and manual laboratory testing across various departments
Analyze, verify, and report patient results accurately and within established turnaround times
Conduct quality control, quality assurance, and proficiency testing activities
Troubleshoot instrumentation, testing methodologies, and technical issues independently
Perform equipment maintenance, calibration, and routine performance checks
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and laboratory standards
Collaborate with physicians, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory personnel to support patient care
Maintain accurate laboratory documentation and patient records
Participate in process improvement initiatives and daily laboratory operations
Help uphold the highest standards of laboratory quality, efficiency, and patient safety

Required Credentials

Qualifications We're Looking For

Active California Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) License
Bachelor's Degree in Clinical Laboratory Science, Medical Technology, Biology, Chemistry, or related field
Current BLS Certification

of the following areas:

Chemistry (Abbott Alinity)
Hematology (Sysmex XN-3100)
Coagulation (Stago STA-R MAX)

Blood Bank (Ortho Vision SWIFT)

Additional Skills

Strong knowledge of Quality Control (QC), Quality Assurance (QA), and laboratory regulatory standards
Ability to troubleshoot instruments and resolve technical issues independently
Excellent communication and teamwork skills
Strong attention to detail and organizational abilities
Reliable attendance and flexibility to support departmental scheduling needs

Work Environment

This isn't a routine laboratory role. You'll be working in a fast-paced hospital setting where every result matters and every day brings new challenges. You'll collaborate with a dedicated team of healthcare professionals while utilizing advanced instrumentation to support a diverse patient population.

HireArt is helping our client find a Research Associate to join its Learning from Videos (LFV) team and contribute to research advancing world models, video generation, and policy learning capabilities.

You're proactive, self-directed, and comfortable contributing both to cutting-edge research and the high-quality software infrastructure needed to support it.

As Research Associate, You'll

Contribute to research on multimodal and multi-view world models, video generation, video policies, and related areas, including ongoing projects, university partnerships, research meetings, and publications for top-tier conferences.
Contribute to the team's internal video generation codebase, Any4Dv3, by maintaining high-quality code, reviewing pull requests, stress-testing new capabilities, developing new functionality, and supporting ongoing development.
Advance research in world-action models (WAMs) within Any4Dv3 by benchmarking state-of-the-art methods, deploying solutions in simulation and on real robotic hardware, identifying gaps in current technologies, and developing approaches to address them.
Produce maintainable, well-documented code and contribute to internal tooling and open-source releases for the scientific community.

Requirements

Current PhD student in a related field
Strong fundamentals in at least one of the following areas: computer vision, video understanding, generative models, 3D reconstruction, or robotics
Experience with video diffusion models, world models, and world-action models
Proactive and self-directed, with the ability to operate effectively in a research-driven environment
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to take ownership of problems from end to end

Bonus Qualifications

A track record of contributions to open-source projects or publications at top-tier venues such as CVPR, ICLR, NeurIPS, RSS, or ICRA

This is a part-time (20 hours per week), 6-month contract position staffed via HireArt. It will be onsite and available to candidates local to the Los Altos, CA area.

jobs.title: Life Sciences Supply Chain Manufacturing Ops & AI Transformation Delivery- Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Client-facing Life Sciences manufacturing transformation leader accountable for shaping and delivering technology-enabled programs that improve manufacturing performance, quality, compliance, and supply reliability. The role combines regulated plant-floor expertise with data, AI, automation, and disciplined program delivery.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Manager in Supply Chain Manufacturing, you will lead transformation programs for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical-device manufacturers, from defining the operational problem and value case through solution design, implementation, adoption, stabilization, and measurable results. You will work across manufacturing, quality, laboratory, engineering, supply chain, and technology teams to connect plant operations with enterprise systems and data.

This is a techno-functional delivery role. You will need the credibility to redesign manufacturing processes and operating models, and the fluency to direct teams delivering manufacturing execution, automation, integration, data, and AI solutions. You will remain accountable for delivery quality, risk, client relationships, and outcomes in regulated environments. “The Life Sciences focus reflects the practice’s emphasis on connected manufacturing and quality workflows across process, batch, and discrete operations, including electronic batch records, electronic device history records (eDHRs), traceability, and integration across plant and enterprise systems.”

Your Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will lead complex client engagements while balancing operational improvement, technology delivery, quality requirements, and commercial commitments. You will:

Lead end-to-end Life Sciences manufacturing transformations, from assessment and mobilization through design, deployment, stabilization, and value realization.
Build trusted relationships with senior manufacturing, quality, MS&T, engineering, supply chain, digital, and IT/OT stakeholders; establish governance and drive timely decisions.
Translate priorities such as yield, throughput, right-first-time execution, deviation reduction, batch-cycle time, asset reliability, and supply continuity into practical workplans and outcome measures.
Direct multidisciplinary teams across manufacturing process design, MES/MOM, automation, data engineering, AI, architecture, integration, quality, change management, testing, and deployment.
Lead solution and process design for batch and discrete execution, electronic batch records, electronic device history records (eDHRs), recipes and routings, material and product genealogy, review by exception, maintenance, quality workflows, and plant performance management.
Guide integration across MES/MOM, ERP, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, asset-management systems, and relevant cloud or edge platforms.
Establish trusted manufacturing data foundations through appropriate data models, asset and process context, master data, metadata, lineage, governance, and secure IT/OT connectivity.
Shape analytics and AI use cases, such as process monitoring, predictive maintenance, deviation investigation support, digital twins, and decision support; assess their value, data readiness, workflow fit, and risks before scaling.
Partner with client quality and validation teams to incorporate applicable GxP controls, data integrity, electronic-record requirements, change control, and risk-based assurance into delivery plans. The applicable controls will depend on the product, system, and intended use.
Manage scope, schedule, budget, staffing, dependencies, quality, risks, issues, and contractual commitments; guide testing, cutover, training, adoption, and operational handover.
Connect digital solutions to daily management, operational excellence, workforce capability building, and sustained process improvement.
Ability to create clarity and alignment across distributed teams, motivate people through complex delivery challenges, and maintain accountability without becoming the bottleneck for decisions.
People leadership and talent-development capability, including coaching, delegation, performance feedback, conflict resolution, succession planning, and building teams with the right mix of functional, technical, and industry skills.
Develop Managers and delivery teams, contribute reusable methods and lessons learned, and identify appropriate follow-on opportunities with account teams.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Success in this role requires the ability to connect regulated manufacturing realities with scalable technology delivery. You will bring:

Strong knowledge of Life Sciences manufacturing processes and the relationship between production, quality, laboratory operations, engineering, and supply.
Techno-functional leadership that earns the confidence of plant teams while providing clear direction to architects, engineers, developers, data scientists, and cybersecurity specialists.
Working knowledge of industrial data and integration patterns, including OPC UA (IEC 62541), MQTT/Sparkplug, APIs, historians, asset and batch contextualization, and unified-namespace approaches; able to evaluate how these patterns support secure, reliable data exchange across OT and enterprise systems.
Sound judgment about where analytics or AI can improve a workflow, what evidence is needed to support its use, and where human review and quality oversight must remain.
Executive communication, structured problem-solving, facilitation, negotiation, and the ability to make decisions under ambiguity.
Commercial and delivery discipline across estimates, staffing, engagement economics, change control, risk management, and value realization.

To qualify for the role, you must have:

A bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, manufacturing, supply chain, information systems, business, or a related discipline.
No less than 10+ years of relevant experience spanning Life Sciences manufacturing, manufacturing technology, operational excellence, industrial data and AI, technology consulting, or a related field.
Experience leading complex manufacturing transformation or technology-enabled improvement initiatives in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device, or comparably regulated environment.
Experience delivering client-facing programs through design, implementation, deployment, and stabilization, with accountability for governance, resources, quality, financial performance, and risk.
Experience leading senior stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams across business, functional, data, and technology workstreams.
Experience translating manufacturing requirements into process, system, data, integration, security, and technical requirements, with traceability through testing and deployment.
Practical understanding of GxP manufacturing and the quality, documentation, change-control, and data-integrity considerations relevant to digital solutions.
Ability to travel as needed based on business and role requirements. Travel can range from 80-100%.

Ideally, you’ll also have:

Experience with drug substance, drug product, biologics, sterile manufacturing, medical devices, or clinical-to-commercial scale-up.
Experience leading multi-site deployments, greenfield or brownfield plant modernization, or manufacturing technology-transfer initiatives.
Implementation experience with one or more MES/MOM platforms, electronic batch records and eDHRs, recipe management, connected-worker tools, industrial analytics, or manufacturing data platforms.
Familiarity with ISA-88/IEC 61512, ISA-95/IEC 62264, OPC UA/IEC 62541, and OT cybersecurity practices informed by ISA/IEC 62443 and NIST SP 800-82. Exposure to IEC 61131-3, IEC 61499, CESMII i3X, O-PAS, or SiLA 2 is a plus where relevant to the client environment.
Familiarity with Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and continuous-improvement practices, and their application to manufacturing analytics, process performance, quality, and operational decision-making.
Experience with computer system validation or risk-based computer software assurance, as applicable to the systems and regulated products involved.
Experience applying AI or advanced analytics to manufacturing or quality workflows with appropriate model governance, monitoring, and human oversight.
A master’s degree or relevant program-management, operational-excellence, cloud, data, or manufacturing-technology certification.

What We Look For

We are looking for a Senior Manager who can move confidently between the plant floor and the executive discussion. The successful candidate will combine Life Sciences manufacturing credibility, quality-minded judgment, technology and data fluency, commercial awareness, and hands-on delivery leadership to produce improvements that clients can operate and sustain.

What We Offer You

At EY, we harness our collective strength to empower you to shape your future with confidence through professional growth, personal fulfillment and an inclusive culture. Learn more at ey.com/us/careers.

The salary range for this job is:
New York City, Boston, and Washington DC Metro Areas, Washington State, and Southern California offices – $180,500 to $374,800

Individual salaries within these ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.

Translate priorities such as yield, throughput, right-first-time execution, batch-cycle time, deviation reduction, asset reliability, and supply continuity into process designs, requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable improvements.

Practical understanding of Life Sciences manufacturing and the connections among production, quality, laboratory operations, engineering, and supply chain.

Sound judgment about when analytics or AI is useful, what data and controls it requires, and how people will use its outputs in manufacturing or quality workflows.
Strong workshop facilitation, structured problem-solving, client communication, team coordination, and delivery-risk management skills.

A bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, manufacturing, supply chain, information systems, business, or a related discipline.

Experience leading a client-facing manufacturing, digital, data, or technology workstream through design and at least one implementation or deployment phase.
Experience working in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device, or comparably regulated manufacturing environment.
Experience translating manufacturing needs into process, functional, data, integration, or testing deliverables and coordinating business and technical contributors.
Practical understanding of GxP manufacturing and the documentation, change-control, quality, and data-integrity considerations relevant to digital solutions.

Experience with drug substance, drug product, biologics, sterile manufacturing, medical devices, or clinical-to-commercial scale-up.

The role combines practical knowledge of manufacturing processes with hands-on skills in manufacturing systems, industrial data, integration, analytics, and AI-enabled workflows.

The Opportunity

As a Senior in Supply Chain Manufacturing, you will work with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical-device clients to connect production, quality, laboratory, engineering, and supply chain needs with deployable technology. You will contribute across the delivery lifecycle, from plant and system assessments through requirements, solution design, configuration support, testing, deployment, adoption, and stabilization.

You will work directly with operators, engineers, quality teams, IT and OT specialists, data teams, and technology providers. You will own assigned technical and functional deliverables, help resolve implementation issues, and make clear recommendations to your workstream lead. The role calls for someone who can examine a shop-floor workflow, trace the data and systems behind it, and turn what they learn into a design or testable requirement.

Your Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

Assess manufacturing and quality workflows, user needs, system interfaces, equipment data, and current-state pain points through site observations, interviews, workshops, and data review.
Document process flows, user stories, functional requirements, data mappings, interface requirements, controls, and acceptance criteria for digital manufacturing solutions.
Support the design and implementation of capabilities such as manufacturing execution, electronic batch records and electronic device history records (eDHRs), recipe and routing management, batch and unit genealogy, review by exception, connected-worker workflows, and plant performance reporting.
Trace information across relevant systems, including MES/MOM, ERP, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, and asset-management platforms; identify data gaps, inconsistent definitions, and integration dependencies.
Develop and review equipment and batch hierarchies, source-to-target mappings, data-quality rules, and contextualized datasets with manufacturing, automation, and data specialists.
Work with solution architects and engineers on interface specifications, APIs, industrial connectivity, and the movement of data between plant, edge, and enterprise environments.
Configure or prototype solution components where appropriate to your experience and the engagement, and document design decisions for review by technical and client leads.
Prepare and execute functional and integration test scripts, record defects, support resolution and retesting, and maintain traceability between requirements and test evidence.
Support deployment readiness, cutover, user training, hypercare, and handover by preparing clear technical documentation and responding to issues from plant users.
Partner with client quality and validation teams to prepare or review applicable documentation concerning GxP, data integrity, electronic records, change control, and computer system validation or risk-based assurance.
Contribute to analytics and AI use cases by assessing source-data quality, defining manufacturing context, checking outputs against operational workflows, and documenting where human review is needed.

jobs.title: Life Sciences Supply Chain Manufacturing Ops & AI Transformation Delivery - Senior
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Role Snapshot

Client-facing Life Sciences manufacturing professional who helps design, build, test, and deploy digital solutions for regulated plant operations. The role combines practical knowledge of manufacturing processes with hands-on skills in manufacturing systems, industrial data, integration, analytics, and AI-enabled workflows.

The Opportunity

As a Senior in Supply Chain Manufacturing, you will work with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical-device clients to connect production, quality, laboratory, engineering, and supply chain needs with deployable technology. You will contribute across the delivery lifecycle, from plant and system assessments through requirements, solution design, configuration support, testing, deployment, adoption, and stabilization.

You will work directly with operators, engineers, quality teams, IT and OT specialists, data teams, and technology providers. You will own assigned technical and functional deliverables, help resolve implementation issues, and make clear recommendations to your workstream lead. The role calls for someone who can examine a shop-floor workflow, trace the data and systems behind it, and turn what they learn into a design or testable requirement.

Your Key Responsibilities

In this role, you will:

Assess manufacturing and quality workflows, user needs, system interfaces, equipment data, and current-state pain points through site observations, interviews, workshops, and data review.
Document process flows, user stories, functional requirements, data mappings, interface requirements, controls, and acceptance criteria for digital manufacturing solutions.
Support the design and implementation of capabilities such as manufacturing execution, electronic batch records and electronic device history records (eDHRs), recipe and routing management, batch and unit genealogy, review by exception, connected-worker workflows, and plant performance reporting.
Trace information across relevant systems, including MES/MOM, ERP, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, and asset-management platforms; identify data gaps, inconsistent definitions, and integration dependencies.
Develop and review equipment and batch hierarchies, source-to-target mappings, data-quality rules, and contextualized datasets with manufacturing, automation, and data specialists.
Work with solution architects and engineers on interface specifications, APIs, industrial connectivity, and the movement of data between plant, edge, and enterprise environments.
Configure or prototype solution components where appropriate to your experience and the engagement, and document design decisions for review by technical and client leads.
Prepare and execute functional and integration test scripts, record defects, support resolution and retesting, and maintain traceability between requirements and test evidence.
Support deployment readiness, cutover, user training, hypercare, and handover by preparing clear technical documentation and responding to issues from plant users.
Partner with client quality and validation teams to prepare or review applicable documentation concerning GxP, data integrity, electronic records, change control, and computer system validation or risk-based assurance.
Contribute to analytics and AI use cases by assessing source-data quality, defining manufacturing context, checking outputs against operational workflows, and documenting where human review is needed.
Communicate progress, risks, dependencies, and recommended next steps to client counterparts and engagement leaders; coordinate defined tasks with junior colleagues when needed.

Skills And Attributes For Success

To thrive in this role, you should be able to work in depth in at least one technical area while collaborating across the broader manufacturing solution. You will bring:

Manufacturing and quality understanding: Knowledge of how production execution, batch records, equipment, materials, laboratory results, deviations, and quality review connect in a regulated plant.
Manufacturing technology skills: Hands-on functional, configuration, integration, testing, or support experience with one or more manufacturing, quality, laboratory, automation, or industrial-data solutions.
Data and integration skills: Ability to identify source systems, interpret batch and equipment data, document mappings and interfaces, investigate data-quality issues, and explain how information moves between OT and enterprise systems.
Delivery discipline: Ability to produce accurate requirements, design documents, test scripts, defect records, and deployment materials, and to follow issues through resolution.
Technical communication: Ability to discuss an operational problem with a plant user and document it clearly enough for a developer, data engineer, automation specialist, or tester to act on.
Regulated-delivery awareness: Understanding of why documentation, traceability, controlled changes, and reliable data matter when a solution supports GxP activities.
Analytical judgment: Curiosity about AI and advanced analytics, paired with the ability to test whether the underlying data, workflow, and proposed output are fit for use.

To qualify for the role, you must have:

A bachelor’s degree in engineering, life sciences, manufacturing, information systems, computer science, supply chain, or a related discipline.
At least 3 years of relevant experience in Life Sciences manufacturing, manufacturing systems, automation, industrial data, systems implementation, technology consulting, or a related field.
Experience working with manufacturing or quality processes in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device, or comparably regulated environment.
Experience producing technical or functional delivery artifacts, such as requirements, process maps, data mappings, interface specifications, configuration documents, test scripts, or deployment materials.
Experience collaborating with both operational stakeholders and technical delivery teams to investigate requirements, resolve issues, or implement a solution.
Ability to travel as needed based on business and role requirements. Travel can range from 80-100%.

Ideally, you’ll also have:

Experience with MES/MOM, electronic batch records or eDHRs, recipe management, LIMS, QMS, historians, SCADA, DCS/PLC, connected-worker solutions, or industrial data platforms.
Experience examining manufacturing data from more than one source and relating it to assets, materials, products, orders, recipes, batches, or quality events.
Familiarity with ISA-88/IEC 61512 batch concepts, ISA-95/IEC 62264 manufacturing information models, or industrial connectivity approaches such as OPC UA and MQTT/Sparkplug.
Exposure to GxP computer system validation, risk-based software assurance, data-integrity controls, electronic records, or OT cybersecurity considerations relevant to the system being delivered.
Familiarity with Process Analytical Technology (PAT) and continuous improvement practices, including the use of manufacturing data to monitor process performance, identify variability, and improve quality, throughput, and operational performance.
Experience supporting analytics or AI use cases in manufacturing or quality, such as process monitoring, predictive maintenance, deviation investigation, or decision support.
Experience with drug substance, drug product, biologics, sterile manufacturing, medical devices, or technology transfer.
Relevant platform, cloud, data, automation, Agile, or manufacturing certification.

What We Look For

We are looking for a Senior who enjoys getting close to the manufacturing process and the technology that supports it. The strongest candidates ask precise questions, produce dependable technical work, recognize when data or design assumptions do not hold up, and collaborate well with plant, quality, and technology teams to make solutions usable in practice.

Our Mission:
Hospital-Quality Care, Everywhere.

The healthcare industry still relies on faxes and phone tags to coordinate critical care for patients at home. We think patients and the clinicians who serve them deserve better than a system stuck in 1995.

Verse Medical is building the modern software infrastructure to make it happen. We're a well-funded Series C company (backed by General Catalyst, SignalFire, and Sapphire Ventures) on a mission to heal a fragmented system. Our platform connects the dots between providers, payors, and patients, ensuring people get the high-quality care they need, reliably and right where they live. We’re growing fast and looking for people who are driven by this mission to join us!

Our Values:
The Principles That Guide Us

Our values are the operating system for how we work together and with our partners. They aren't just words on a wall; they are the principles we bring to every decision, every day.

We are transparent, upfront and direct. We operate with honesty and clarity. We share information openly, the good and the bad, and believe that direct, respectful feedback is the foundation of trust and progress.
We value speed of iteration. We are building something new, which means we learn by doing. We prioritize rapid iteration and getting solutions into the hands of users, believing that progress is more valuable than perfection.
We give 110% effort, 30% of the time. We are passionate about our mission, and there are moments that require us to go the extra mile. We believe in focused intensity when it counts, balanced by a sustainable pace that keeps our team energized for the long run.
We empathize with customers to a fault. When our users face a problem, we own it. Instead of asking them to change, we ask ourselves, "How can we make this better?" We believe true innovation comes from deep empathy and a relentless focus on solving the real-world challenges of healthcare.

We’re hiring a Data Analyst
to turn Verse's data into decisions. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role where you'll partner directly with functional leaders to build the metrics, dashboards, and analyses that drive how the business operates. Not only are you offering the “what,” but also the “why” and the “what now,” translating messy, ambiguous business questions into clear, defensible, self-serve analytical assets.

If you enjoy high ownership, solving open-ended business problems with data, and having direct influence on a mission-driven company’s trajectory, this role is for you.

What You'll Achieve: A Glimpse into Your Contributions

Spearhead end-to-end analytics across business domains.
Understand trends in operational and customer data to influence how teams prioritize their own roadmaps
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Ops, Product, Leadership) to define new metrics, standardize reporting, and surface insights proactively.
Automate recurring reporting and manual data-quality checks using Python and SQL, reducing turnaround time on regular audits and deliverables.
Design and build algorithms/models (e.g., scoring, classification, similarity, or risk-adjustment models) that solve specific business problems, from provider mapping to fraud detection to cost-of-care scoring.

What You'll Bring: The Skills and Experience You’ll Leverage

We believe that diverse experiences and backgrounds lead to better solutions. While we have an idea of what will help someone succeed in this role, we are open to being convinced by your unique story and skills. If you believe you can achieve the outcomes above, we encourage you to apply.

Core Skills & Experience:

3+ years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or analytics engineering, with experience owning reporting and metrics end-to-end.
Strong experience writing SQL and Python for analysis, automation, and lightweight modeling
Experience building and driving adoption of dashboards (Metabase, Looker Tableau, PowerBI, or similar)
Experience developing custom metrics, scoring algorithms, or classification models to solve specific business problems.
Experience performing exploratory analysis with minimal direction on ambiguous, open-ended business questions
Proactive communicator with experience working with stakeholders
Preferred: Experience with dbt modeling.
Preferred: Experience with Snowflake.
Preferred: Familiarity with healthcare or other regulated data (HIPAA compliance).
Preferred: Experience working closely with engineers to triage and resolve issues.

Benefits:

Competitive compensation.
Opportunities for rapid career advancement in a growing company.
100% premium coverage for health insurance.
401(k) with no matching at this time.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York office and will require you to be in the office 4x in a week.

Our Pledge for an Equitable Future

At Verse Medical, our mission is to deliver equitable, hospital-quality care to everyone, regardless of their background or where they live. We can only achieve this if our own team reflects the diversity of the patients we serve. We are committed to building a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, where their contributions are valued, and where they can do their best work. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

About The Team

The Growth Data Science team partners closely with Product, Marketing, Sales, and regional business leaders to identify growth opportunities across the customer lifecycle—from acquisition and activation to conversion, retention, and expansion. Technical Due Diligence Subject Matter Expert

Location:
Remote – EU-based candidates preferred
Languages:
Spanish, Hungarian, or French (fluency in at least one required)
Job Description

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Technical Due Diligence Subject Matter Expert with fluency in French, Finnish, Hungarian, or German (written and verbal) to personally inspect and evaluate the architecture, code, and technical roadmaps of target companies during investment and acquisition processes. This is not a management-level advisory role — the client is specifically looking for someone who can get into the technical details themselves, rather than relying on self-reported management summaries, to uncover risks that wouldn't otherwise surface. The ideal candidate combines deep, current engineering judgment with the ability to translate technical findings into quantified business and investment impact.
Key Responsibilities

Hands-On Technical Investigation:

Personally inspect codebases, system architecture, infrastructure, and technical roadmaps to directly assess engineering quality — not solely through management interviews or self-reported documentation.
Engineering Judgment & Risk Identification:

Independently distinguish sound architecture from weak or fragile architecture, and identify hidden risks such as undisclosed systems, accumulated technical debt, unrealistic roadmaps, and structural weaknesses that may not be visible at a management level.
Risk Assessment & Reporting:

Provide a structured evaluation of technical debt, security gaps, operational risks, business interruption risks, and talent gaps, grounded in direct technical review.
Business/Investment Impact Quantification:

Translate technical findings into quantified business and investment impact — for example, identifying a specific technical issue that materially affects valuation — to directly inform deal decisions.
Validation & Assumption Testing:

Validate findings against business assumptions and provide recommendations on critical areas requiring attention.
Findings Categorization:

Document and classify findings into Deal Blockers, Material Findings, and Non-Material Findings with clear, evidence-based justifications.
Comprehensive Documentation:

Produce detailed TDD reports covering product, people, technology, and processes, giving a complete, technically grounded overview of the target company's technical landscape.
Process Improvement:

Recommend best practices to enhance the efficiency and rigor of the due diligence process.
Stakeholder Communication:

Present findings and recommendations to investors, executives, and decision-makers clearly and actionably, including the business/financial implications of technical findings.
Key Qualifications

15+ years of hands-on technology experience, with a track record of remaining personally close to code, architecture, and implementation details (not purely a management or oversight background).
Proven track record conducting hands-on technical due diligence for acquisitions, investments, or technology assessments — including direct code and architecture review, not just management-level evaluation.
Deep expertise in software architecture, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, cybersecurity, and software development lifecycle (SDLC).
Strong, current engineering judgment — demonstrated ability to independently evaluate architecture quality without relying on management reports.
Strong understanding of technical debt, scalability challenges, and operational risks, with the ability to quantify their business and investment impact.
Experience with modern development stacks and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP).
Exceptional analytical and documentation skills, with experience writing due diligence reports that connect technical findings to financial/valuation outcomes.
Strong ability to communicate complex technical findings to non-technical stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Type of Appointment:
Full-time, Probationary (10/12 Schedule)

Job Classification:
Phlebotomy/Clinical Lab Assistant

Anticipated Hiring Range:
$3,147 - $3,761 per month

The Department

Student Health Services is one component of the Campus Health and Wellbeing Cluster within the Division of Student Affairs. This new cluster stresses the University's commitment to preventative and holistic approaches to wellbeing in support of students and the institution's mission and strategic plan. The mission of Student Health Services is to promote students' healthy lifestyles and academic success by providing quality medical, psychological, and wellness services. The department provides ambulatory health care, health education programs, prevention, and healing services to students of Cal Poly Pomona.

Duties And Responsibilities

Under the supervision of a general Clinical Lab Scientist (CLS I & CLS II), performs the following: Phlebotomy, Specimen Collection, and Patient Care

Greets patients, verifies identity using approved identifiers, confirms laboratory orders, and prepares patients for specimen collection.
Explains collection procedures and provides instructions regarding fasting, timed collections, clean-catch urine specimens, and other testing requirements.
Performs venipuncture and capillary phlebotomy in accordance with established procedures and within the scope of applicable certification.
Selects the appropriate collection tube, container, specimen type, and required volume for each ordered test.
Collects blood, urine, and other authorized specimens while maintaining patient comfort, privacy, and safety.
Observes patients for adverse reactions, including dizziness or fainting, and follows established response and notification procedures.
Provides professional, compassionate, and student-centered service throughout the laboratory visit.

Specimen Processing, Storage, and Transport

Accurately labels specimens at the time of collection and verifies that identifiers match the laboratory order and accompanying documentation.
Determines whether testing will be performed in-house or sent to a reference laboratory.
Completes laboratory requisitions, labels, logs, and other required documentation accurately.
Processes specimens according to established requirements, including centrifuging, separating, aliquoting, packaging, and preparing specimens for testing or transport.
Preserves and stores specimens according to test-specific temperature, timing, light-protection, and stability requirements.
Maintains specimen integrity throughout collection, processing, storage, and transport.
Coordinates reference-laboratory pickups and ensures specimens are packaged and transported within established timeframes.
Identifies mislabeled, insufficient, compromised, leaking, or otherwise unacceptable specimens and promptly reports concerns to the appropriate laboratory or clinical personnel.

Waived Testing and Clinical Laboratory Support

Performs authorized CLIA-waived testing, such as urine dipsticks, hemoglobin A1C, glucose, pregnancy testing, and other approved tests, after completing required training and competency assessments.
Follows approved procedures and manufacturer instructions for test performance, quality control, documentation, and reporting.
Verifies that testing materials have been properly stored and are within their expiration dates before use.
Records reagent lot numbers, expiration dates, quality-control results, and patient test results accurately.
Documents test results in the electronic medical record or applicable laboratory information system.
Immediately refers abnormal, critical, questionable, or inconsistent results to the appropriate licensed clinical or laboratory professional.
Assists laboratory personnel with daily operations and performs other laboratory-support activities within the position’s authorized scope.

Cleaning, Infection Prevention, and Safety

Maintains clean, organized, secure, and appropriately prepared specimen-collection and laboratory work areas.
Cleans and disinfects collection chairs, counters, equipment, and other work surfaces according to established schedules and procedures.
Uses appropriate personal protective equipment and follows standard precautions during all patient-care and laboratory activities.
Handles and disposes of sharps, biohazardous materials, chemicals, and regulated waste safely and in accordance with established requirements.
Maintains continual awareness of the laboratory environment and promptly identifies and reports potential hazards or unsafe conditions. Follows established procedures for needlestick injuries, blood or body-fluid exposures, spills, emergencies, and incident reporting.
Helps maintain a safe, secure, and healthy patient-care environment by adhering to organizational standards, policies, and legal requirements.

Equipment, Inventory, and Opening/Closing Duties

Monitors phlebotomy and laboratory supplies to maintain sufficient inventory levels for daily operations.
Receives, organizes, rotates, and stocks supplies using applicable expiration-date and first-expire, first-out practices.
Checks collection supplies, reagents, and testing materials for proper storage, condition, lot numbers, and expiration dates.
Reports supply shortages and assists with preparing inventory or ordering requests.
Performs assigned daily opening and closing procedures for laboratory and specimen-collection areas.
Verifies that work areas, equipment, and supplies are clean, functional, properly stored, and ready for patient care.
Completes required refrigerator, freezer, and room-temperature checks, equipment checks, and laboratory logs.
Secures specimens, confidential records, supplies, equipment, and laboratory areas at the end of the workday.
Reports unresolved equipment, temperature, safety, supply, or specimen concerns to the appropriate laboratory or clinical personnel.

Documentation, Compliance, and Quality Assurance

Accurately documents specimen collection, processing, waived testing, and specimen disposition in the electronic medical record and applicable laboratory logs.
Maintains complete, accurate, and legible records required for patient care, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance.
Protects confidential health information and maintains patient privacy in accordance with HIPAA, FERPA, organizational policies, and applicable laws.
Complies with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including CLIA, OSHA, bloodborne-pathogen standards, and Student Health Services policies and procedures.
Participates in required training, competency assessments, continuing education, quality-assurance activities, audits, and inspections.
Completes required quality-control, temperature, maintenance, specimen, and corrective-action logs.
Identifies and reports documentation errors, specimen discrepancies, safety concerns, equipment problems, and potential regulatory issues.

Qualifications

Combination - High school diploma or equivalent and six to twelve months of related experience in a healthcare setting or equivalent combination of education and experience which provides the required knowledge and abilities.
CPT I - Certified Phlebotomy Technician Level I: Possess and maintain valid certification as a Certified Phlebotomy Technician I, as defined by the California Department of Health Services, which permits the incumbent to perform skin punctures and venipuncture.
Six to twelve months of related experience in a healthcare setting or equivalent combination of education and experience which provides the required knowledge and abilities.
Knowledge: General knowledge of clinical laboratory operations and equipment, including an understanding of, or the ability to quickly learn, laboratory safety and quality assurance practices and procedures. General knowledge of medical terminology pertinent to laboratory operations; applicable laws and regulations pertaining to clinical laboratory operations and patient confidentiality. Working knowledge of CLIA-waived testing procedures, methods, and criteria. Abilities: Ability to collect required specimens for and perform assigned CLIA-waived testing with required attention to accuracy and detail; perform phlebotomy using the appropriate equipment including venipuncture and capillary puncture; use applicable equipment and materials in performing laboratory tests; use applicable automated systems for maintaining and tracking laboratory and patient records; maintain patient confidentiality as required by applicable state and federal laws and regulations; maintain effective working relationships with practitioners and other health center support staff; and be sensitive to and communicate effectively with diverse patients.

Preferred Qualifications

Must have basic knowledge of biomedical science for the performance of pre-testing preparations in all laboratory areas.
Must be able to type and operate basic office equipment and be familiar with computer operation.
Familiarity with the principles of basic laboratory equipment used in pre-testing is preferred.
High school diploma or equivalent.
Possess and maintain valid certification as a Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (Collect and process specimens via phlebotomy, including venipuncture and capillary puncture and perform basic and CLIA-waived testing).
One year of experience working in a clinical laboratory or healthcare setting as a Certified Phlebotomy Technician I

jobs.title: Laboratory Technician - Immunoassays
jobs.description:
About ChronicleBio

ChronicleBio is a clinical-stage precision techbio company developing biomarker-guided treatments for ME/CFS, Long COVID, POTS, and related neuroimmune conditions. Our platform combines a large-scale biobank with an endotype-driven diagnostic and therapeutic strategy, allowing us to match existing and novel therapeutics to the specific drivers of each patient's disease. We are a mission-driven team aiming to lead discovery in the largest unmet needs in healthcare.

The Role

ChronicleBio seeks a Research Associate to run plate-based immunoassays on human biospecimens for our biomarker research programs. You will handle day-to-day assay execution, from sample prep through data QC and reporting. This bench-focused role suits someone who values clean technique, careful sample tracking, and reproducible data.

Key Responsibilities

Run ELISAs and related immunoassays in duplicate according to kit inserts and internal SOPs, keeping incubation times and temperatures exact.
Prepare buffers, standards, controls, and reagents; thaw, aliquot, and dilute plasma and serum samples.
Lay out and wash plates (manually or with an automated washer), and pipette accurately with multichannel pipettes on a tight schedule.
Read plates on a microplate reader, fit standard curves, calculate results, and apply QC criteria (curve fit, %CV, controls); re-run samples that fail QC or fall out of range.
Keep sample inventory, chain of custody, reagent lot numbers, and raw data up to date in the LIMS/ELN; report status and issues to the supervising scientist.
Help troubleshoot assays, and help onboard new kits or protocols as project needs change.
Handle human biospecimens safely under BSL-2 and Universal Precautions.

What You Bring

B.S. in Biology, Biochemistry, Immunology, or a related field, with 1+ year of hands-on lab experience.
Proven experience running ELISAs or similar plate-based immunoassays end to end, including standard curve analysis in Excel, Prism, or similar software.
Strong single- and multichannel pipetting skills; experience handling human plasma or serum under BSL-2.
Attention to detail and reliable documentation and sample traceability.

jobs.description:
Description

Position Summary

Avum is seeking a Senior DoD Contracting Subject Matter Expert with at least 15 years of experience supporting Federal or Department of Defense acquisition and contracting activities.

This individual will provide functional expertise to support the design, implementation, sustainment, and improvement of procurement business systems. Working closely with software developers, business analysts, QA teams, and government stakeholders, the SME will translate contracting regulations, business processes, and user needs into clear software requirements.

The ideal candidate has extensive knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and the federal contracting lifecycle, along with hands-on experience using procurement systems. This role focuses on helping technical teams build and support solutions that meet the operational needs of contracting personnel.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the senior functional resource for Federal and DoD acquisition and contracting workflows, business processes, and procurement system requirements.
Work with contracting personnel and government stakeholders to identify user needs, clarify requirements, and resolve functional questions.
Translate FAR, DFARS, and applicable agency requirements into functional requirements, business rules, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Provide expertise across the contracting lifecycle, including acquisition planning, solicitations, evaluations, awards, modifications, contract administration, and closeout.
Review system designs and proposed software functionality for alignment with contracting processes and user needs.
Support Agile development teams through requirements refinement, sprint planning, demonstrations, and functional reviews.
Develop and review functional test scenarios, support user acceptance testing, and validate that software features meet documented requirements.
Assess existing procurement processes and recommend improvements through updated workflows, automation, and system enhancements.
Support procurement data analysis, reporting requirements, and validation of system outputs.
Provide functional support for data migration, including mapping, interpretation, and validation of contracting data.
Assist Tier 3 service desk personnel with complex procurement system issues, workflow questions, and functional troubleshooting.
Develop and review user guides, training materials, business process documentation, and knowledge base content.
Explain complex contracting requirements clearly to technical teams and stakeholders with varying levels of procurement experience.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $115,000 to $150,000 annually. Actual compensation and position level will be determined based on experience, qualifications, certifications, geographic location, and the responsibilities of the assigned role.

Avum offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical (Cigna), dental and vision (Principal), 401(k), PTO, education reimbursement, and certification reimbursement.

Work Environment & Requirements

Hybrid/remote work environment with potential on-site requirements based on contract needs
U.S. citizenship required.
Active Secret security clearance or the ability to obtain and maintain one, consistent with contract requirements. An appropriate active clearance and authorized access are required before performing classified duties.
Background investigation required.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Avum, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected class under federal, state, or local law. Avum is committed to compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and VEVRAA, and maintains an active Affirmative Action Plan.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

At least 15 years of professional experience in Federal or DoD acquisition and contracting, including direct experience with contracting workflows, procurement processes, and contract lifecycle activities.
Extensive working knowledge of FAR and DFARS and experience applying these requirements to Federal or DoD contracting activities.
Hands-on experience using federal procurement or contract writing systems, such as PD2/SPS, CONWRITE, PIEE, WAWF, or comparable agency systems.
Ability to translate contracting policies, procedures, and operational needs into clear functional requirements and business rules.
Experience reviewing procurement workflows, identifying process gaps, and recommending practical improvements.
Ability to validate system functionality and data against contracting requirements and expected business outcomes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain contracting concepts to software developers and other technical personnel.
Ability to work independently and collaborate with government stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams in a remote environment.
U.S. citizenship required.
Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance. An active Secret clearance is preferred.
Ability to successfully complete the required background investigation.

Preferred Qualifications

Current or previous experience as a Federal 1102 Contract Specialist or Contracting Officer.
Current or previous possession of a Contracting Officer warrant.
Experience supporting DoD procurement system modernization, implementation, or sustainment.
Experience working with software development teams as a functional SME, business analyst, or product stakeholder.
Experience developing user stories, acceptance criteria, functional test scenarios, or user acceptance testing materials.
Familiarity with Agile development practices and tools such as Jira.
Familiarity with the Procurement Data Standard (PDS), procurement system interfaces, and contracting data migration.

Job Summary:

Prioritizes and performs a wide variety of clinical laboratory tests on various biological specimens. Reviews, evaluates, documents and reports results. Preserves confidentiality of patients and follows lab safety and maintenance protocols. Trains and supervises trainees, laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.

**RECRUITMENT ID: 480**

**RESIDENCY**: Candidate must be a California resident. Chico State Enterprises is not a sponsoring agency for staff and management positions (i.e., H-1B Visas).

**POSITION SUMMARY:** This research assistant position supports a Food as Medicine (FAM) Feasibility and Pilot Design under an ARI-funded grant at California State University, Chico. This position is appointed through May 2027 and focuses on evaluating the institutional, policy, operational, and community conditions required to establish and sustain a Food as Medicine initiative in Butte County, utilizing North Valley Food Hub (NVFH) infrastructure. The research assistant will work with the project team to analyze healthcare policy and reimbursement pathways, conduct community asset mapping, synthesize food security needs assessments, and support the co-design of a regional FAM pilot program.

**ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:** In this role, the research assistant will conduct a population needs and nutrition security assessment, evaluating qualitative and quantitative community health data to identify priority populations and gaps in food security across Butte County. This work will culminate in an authored synthesis report evaluating evidence-based FAM implementation models best suited to address local nutritional needs. To complement this assessment, the assistant will apply systems thinking and community asset mapping methodologies by cataloging local food, healthcare, and social service infrastructure. Utilizing visual systems mapping tools (such as Kumu, ArcGIS, or MindManager), the incumbent will visually diagram resource connections, referral networks, and structural relationships across the regional food-health system.

A core component of the position involves stakeholder collaboration and engagement. The research assistant will participate in structured planning deliberations alongside North Valley Food Hub (NVFH) leadership, regional specialty crop producers, institutional procurement representatives, and healthcare partners to foster cross-sector collaboration and identify community strengths and operational barriers to FAM adoption. Concurrently, the research assistant will undertake a healthcare policy and health equity evaluation, examining local, state, and federal policy landscapes—specifically focusing on Medi-Cal/Medicaid reimbursement pathways, procurement incentives, and funding mechanisms—and authoring a report on how these policy environments impact the long-term sustainability of regional FAM programs.

Finally, integrating findings from across all project phases, the research assistant will apply an ecological lens, social justice values, and evidence-based practices to lead evidence-based program planning and pilot design. The incumbent will draft a comprehensive, practical FAM pilot program plan and operational workflow for the North Valley Food Hub, establishing a scalable framework for institutional Food as Medicine partnerships in Northern California.

**EMPLOYMENT STANDARDS:**

Required Qualifications:

* Current enrollment in a Master of Public Health (MPH) program.
* Experience or training in conducting academic literature reviews, policy analysis, and qualitative and/or quantitative data synthesis.

Preferred Qualifications:

jobs.title: Flatiron Research Fellow - Biological Transport Networks, Center for Computational Biology
jobs.description:
Description
The Center for Computational Biology (CCB), an in-house research center of the Simons Foundation ’s Flatiron Institute , is actively seeking enthusiastic, full-time post-doctoral Flatiron Research Fellows to join its Biological Transport & Networks Group .   The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027. Applications will be reviewed beginning in Fall 2026 and considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

ABOUT THE CENTER FOR COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY 

CCB has a twofold mission: to develop the rigorous modeling tools and theory needed for understanding biological processes, and to create computational frameworks that will facilitate the analysis of the large, complex data sets being generated by quantitative experimental technologies. To accomplish this, CCB brings together experts in various biological domains (including genomics, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology) whose approaches are informed by the modern computational tools of applied mathematics, statistical inference, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), biophysics, and computer science. The goal: to enable CCB to undertake ambitious, long-term research projects that transcend conventional disciplinary boundaries and that lead to a quantitative and predictive understanding of biological phenomena; and to develop high-quality, well-tested, versatile and extensible software across its research areas.  

CCB currently comprises more than 50 scientists at career stages from Ph.Ds through senior scientists, as well as visiting scientists and guest researchers, affiliated graduate students and interns. Together, the CCB scientific staff are pioneering an approach to biology in which theory,computation, and experimentation are integrated, from problem conceptualization onwards. This approach enables CCB to tackle not only recognized, fundamental problems in biology that have so far eluded solution, but also, because of the value placed on curiosity-driven research, to find and develop new areas of biological inquiry.

ABOUT THE BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT & NETWORKS GROUP

Led by Eleni Katifori, the Biological Transport Networks group uses theory and computation, in close collaboration with experimentalists, to understand how biological networks develop, remodel, and function. We investigate how local physical processes—including fluid flow, tissue deformation, and transport of nutrients and signaling molecules—give rise to network architecture and collective behavior. Our work connects physics, applied mathematics, and biology, seeking general principles that explain both the diversity of transport networks across organisms and the common constraints that shape their organization.

Current research spans vertebrate vascular development and remodeling, circulation driven by cilia and body contractions in jellyfish, the interplay between tissue mechanics and vascular transport, and transport-informed models of neuronal growth and maturation. Central questions include how adaptation produces hierarchical or looped architectures, how pulsatile flows influence network development and function, and how nonlinearities and vessel compliance affect transport. We combine analytical models, large-scale numerical simulations, artificial intelligence and machine learning methods, and quantitative analysis of experimental data to connect processes at the scale of individual vessels with the behavior of entire networks. Alongside these biological questions, we investigate how adaptive physical networks can learn, store memory, and perform tasks through local interactions, with applications to fluidic and mechanical systems.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Flatiron Research Fellows in CCB are individuals at the postdoctoral level with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas: applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines.

Reporting to the Group Lead, Fellows are expected to carry out an active research program that can be independently directed and/or involve substantial collaboration with other members of CCB or the Flatiron Institute. In addition to their research, Fellows help build the rich scientific community at CCB and the Flatiron Institute by participating in seminars, colloquia, and group meetings; developing their software, mathematical and computational expertise through internal education opportunities; and sharing their knowledge through scientific publications, presentations, and/or software releases, with the financial support of the Institute. Fellows have access to the Flatiron Institute’s powerful scientific computing resources.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Performing theoretical and computational research

Developing, implementing and maintaining scientific software

Participating in the organization of CCB and Flatiron-wide collaborative activities including seminars, workshops and meetings

Participating in the preparation of manuscripts for publication and of presentations at scientific conferences

Assisting in student mentorship

Sharing expertise and providing training and guidance to CCB staff and visitors as needed.

Fellows will be based, and have a principal office or workspace, at the Simons Foundation’s offices in New York City.  The initial appointments for Flatiron Research Fellows are generally for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on performance. FRFs may be eligible for subsidized housing within walking distance of CCB. 
Qualifications
Education

Ph.D. in a relevant field (applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines)

Related Skills & Other Requirements

Demonstrated abilities in mathematical modeling, analysis and/or scientific computation, scientific software and algorithm development, data analysis and inference, and image analysis

Ability to do original and outstanding research in computational biology, and expertise in computational methods, data analysis, software and algorithm development, modeling machine learning, and scientific simulation 

Ability to work well in an interdisciplinary environment, and to collaborate with experimentalists

Strong oral and written communication, data documentation, and presentation skills

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The full-time annual compensation for this position is USD $95,000. In addition to competitive salaries, the Simons Foundation provides employees with an outstanding benefits package.
Application Instructions
To apply, please submit the following via the application portal:

Cover Letter, which should include a summary of applicants’ most significant contributions in graduate school

Curriculum vitae with publications list and, if relevant, links to software 

Research statement of no more than three (3) pages describing the applicant’s past important results, current and future research interests which may include both scientific topics and algorithm and software development, and potential synergies with activities at CCB

Two (2) letters of recommendation 

Applications will generally be reviewed beginning November 2026, and will be considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. For full consideration, candidates are strongly encouraged to submit their complete application by November 30, 2026. 

SELECTION CRITERIA

Applications will be evaluated based on: 

past research accomplishments

the proposed research program

the synergy of applicant’s expertise and research proposal topic with existing CCB staff and research programs, and potential to cross boundaries between CCB groups and/or the Flatiron Institute’s other research centers.

Any queries about the application process or about CCB should be directed to ccbjobs@flatironinstitute.org. Queries about CCB may also be directed to scientific staff at CCB. 

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Application Materials

The Flatiron Institute values authenticity, originality, and transparency throughout the application and hiring process. Applicants are expected to submit application materials that reflect their own original work, experiences, ideas, writing, and scientific or professional judgment. The use of AI-based tools may be appropriate for limited purposes during the hiring process, such as editing, formatting, or code review. However, application materials, including research statements, cover letters, personal statements, and other writing samples, should not be substantially authored or generated by AI systems.

Applicants are encouraged to disclose any significant or material use of AI tools in the preparation of their application materials or throughout the hiring process. The Flatiron Institute does not use AI-based tools to screen applicants.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Our Commitment to Expanding Pathways to Science & Opportunities for All:

Many of the greatest ideas and discoveries come from a diverse mix of minds, backgrounds, and experiences. The Simons Foundation is committed to advancing basic science and mathematics to benefit humankind and expand our collective understanding of our world. As part of our mission, we support partners, programs, and initiatives that seek to broaden the scientific community and open pathways to science and mathematics careers.

Description

Drive transformation for leading Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations while shaping the future of patient care, drug discovery, and clinical innovation through AWS cloud and AI solutions.

Partner with senior leaders at global HCLS enterprises to accelerate their cloud adoption journey, delivering measurable business outcomes and strategic value.

About The Role

Customer Solutions Managers (CSMs) at AWS are obsessed with accelerating customer cloud adoption and driving measurable value from cloud investments. As a CSM in Healthcare & Life Sciences, you'll partner with senior leaders and engineering teams at global organizations to strategize and manage their end-to-end cloud and AI transformation journeys.

We help Healthcare & Life Sciences organizations adopt advanced cloud and AI solutions while migrating existing workloads to the cloud. Together with customers, we shape and execute strategies to build mindshare and broaden the use of AWS offerings across their enterprises.

If you are excited about the prospect of using your cloud architecture experience to assist our most valuable customers, tackling challenging problems, have a hand in shaping the future of cloud adoption, enhancing and growing your own skills, and having fun, then we would love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

You will be a critical partner to our customers, leveraging your experience with large scale cloud transformations and helping shepherd them through their stages of AWS adoption. Guiding the customer through the operational, educational, and governance aspects of a successful AWS cloud journey.

You will interface with customer and AWS leadership, driving collaboration between the other core account groups (Sales, Support, Solutions Architecture, and Professional Services), product/engineering teams, and customer teams, planning and supporting major workload migrations. You will translate strategic initiatives in the account plan into executable actions, working backwards from our customers key milestones. You will manage cadence by leading the reporting and tracking functions along the way. The execution of education plans, roadmap to business outcome alignments, Executive Briefing Sessions, and go-live events and transitions are a few items owned by the CSM that are critical to the success of our customer’s cloud journey.

You are encouraged to think big, invent and take ownership on customer challenges. You will not only bring the best of AWS/Amazon to our customers, you will proactively help solve the customer’s challenges through new ideas, tools and mechanisms.

Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, be aware of details that matter, have excellent problem-solving abilities, and be exemplary communicators both at the executive and project team level. You will be a peer leader, have the ability to gain stakeholder buy-in, negotiate and lead virtual teams. Your enterprise cloud experience and operational excellence will influence the team’s decisions, provide insight, and help drive secure and robust solutions.

You will evangelize AWS services and influence customers for adopting them. You should be passionate about delivering a great customer experience by deploying AWS solutions and driving innovation, and also be obsessed with contributing to the day-to-day management of customers’ successful migration to AWS.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

You will establish a deep understanding of your customer’s business vision, culture and processes, and evangelize AWS services and influence customers to adopt the right solution at the right time. Customer Solution Managers (CSM) are responsible for four focus areas:

1/Accelerating AWS Adoption through Delivery and Execution

2/Identify & Align on Strategic Opportunities: CSMs work with the Customer Account team to work backwards from the customer to identify and pursue strategic cloud opportunities. These strategic cloud opportunities can include but are not limited to large-scale migrations, GenAI, data and analytics, digital innovation, high performance computing, product innovation, and business agility.

3/Customer Enablement, you will serve as the customer’s cloud journey coach and be the voice of the customer within AWS, evangelizing customer needs to AWS leadership, product, and engineering teams.

4/Implement governance structures to effectively govern both our partnership with the customer, and the customer’s adoption of AWS.

These interconnected focus areas will enable CSMs to effectively drive cloud adoption, pursue strategic growth opportunities, and empower customer success - all of which are critical to achieving the Automotive & Manufacturing IBU’s objectives. By aligning CSM activities, goals, and opportunities under these focus areas, the Automotive & Manufacturing CSM team can ensure a disciplined, customer-centric approach that maximizes business impact and revenue realization for AWS.

CSMs play a critical role supporting account teams/customers throughout the sales process, and the customer's cloud transformation journey, whilst consistently demonstrating measurable value to the customer regardless of engagement model.

CSMs are able to effectively coordinate cross-functional resources, drive disciplined project delivery, and quantify the tangible business benefits that customers realize through their cloud transformation initiatives. This holistic approach to customer engagement, coupled with the CSM's deep understanding of the Automotive & Manufacturing Industry and AWS capabilities; positions CSMs as trusted advisors who can guide customers through every stage of their cloud journey - from initial strategy and planning to migration, modernization, and ongoing optimization.

This position requires 15% - 30% travel across the calendar year to the customer.

Skills & Attributes

Exceptional ability to lead through influence across diverse stakeholder groups

Critical thinking and self-motivation with proven ability to navigate ambiguity

Data-driven decision maker who uses metrics to measure success and drive improvements

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with ability to tailor messaging to different audiences

Innovative mindset with passion for solving complex customer challenges

Travel 15-30% as needed, primarily for customer facing events.

About The Team

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

The HCLS Industries team at AWS is committed to helping customers enable their transformation journeys. Our primary goal is to meet customers where they are and work backwards from their industry-specific needs to transform their business and industry. Our team speaks the language of our customers, focusing on business outcomes and industry use cases in everything we do — whether building products and solutions, selling, delivering, or partnering.

At AWS, we value critical thinking, self-motivation, and the ability to deal with ambiguity. We celebrate innovation, encourage data-driven decision making, and create an environment where diverse perspectives drive better outcomes.

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the 8 description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
